def execute(
    self,
    registry_path: str,
    output_dir="query",
    index_ids: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    z: int = 6,
    threshold=0.01,
    single_query: Optional[str] = None,
    aggregate: bool = False,
    threads: int = 1,
    fast: bool = True,
    is_compressed: bool = False,
    method: str = "seq",
    vec: bool = False,
    keep_query: bool = False,
) -> list[KmindexQueryResult]:
    """Run a query against the kmindex registry.

    Args:
        registry_path (str): Path to the kmindex registry.
        output_dir (str): Output directory for query results.
        index_ids (list[str]): Index IDs to query against; empty list queries all.
        z (int): Z-value (error rate parameter) for kmindex.
        threshold (float): Minimum score threshold for reported hits.
        single_query (str, optional): Query identifier; treats all sequences
            as one query.
        aggregate (bool): Whether to aggregate batch results into a single file.
        threads (int): Number of threads to use.
        fast (bool): Enable fast mode (disabled automatically when
            `is_compressed` is True).
        is_compressed (bool): Whether the index is stored in compressed form.
        method (str): Query method passed to kmindex (e.g. ``"seq"``).
        vec (bool): Use ``jsonl_vec`` output format instead of ``jsonl``.
        keep_query (bool): Copy the query file into ``output_dir``.
    """
    index_ids = index_ids if index_ids is not None else []
    result_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, KMINDEX_QUERY_OUTPUT)
    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    if keep_query:
        shutil.copy(self._path, output_dir)

    # info.yaml is written even on failure, with the error and kmindex output
    info: dict = {}
    try:
        info = (
            KmindexWrapper().query(
                input_registry=registry_path,
                query_file=self._path,
                output_dir=result_dir,
                names=index_ids,
                single_query=single_query,
                aggregate=aggregate,
                threads=threads,
                zvalue=z,
                is_compressed=is_compressed,
                fast=fast and not is_compressed,
                threshold=threshold,
                method=method,
                format="jsonl_vec" if vec else "jsonl",
            )
            or {}
        )
    except Exception as e:
        info = dict(getattr(e, "result", None) or {})
        info["error"] = str(e)
        raise
    finally:
        info["query_file"] = os.path.abspath(self._path)
        self.info = info
        with open(os.path.join(output_dir, "info.yaml"), "w") as f:
            yaml.safe_dump(info, f)

    result: list[KmindexQueryResult] = []

    files = list_result_files(result_dir)
    if not files:
        logger.warning(f"No kmindex result file in {result_dir}")
    for fpath in files:
        try:
            result.append(KmindexQueryResult(fpath, metadata=self.info))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Could not read result from {fpath}: {e}")

    return result

class QueryRunner:
    """Orchestrates one or more kmindex query operations.

    Accepts a list of query file paths (or ``"-"`` for stdin), resolves them to
    concrete files, optionally batches them, and runs each query via
    ``KmindexQuery``.  Output-directory conflict resolution, format conversion,
    and temp-file cleanup are all handled internally.

    Args:
        config: Runtime configuration.  See ``QueryRunnerConfig``.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: QueryRunnerConfig) -> None:
        self._config = config
        # info.yaml of the query in progress, reported on failure
        self._info_path: Optional[str] = None
        if self._config.compressed and self._config.parallel != "sub":
            logger.warning(
                "--compressed requires sub parallelization strategy; "
                "forcing parallel=sub"
            )
            self._config.parallel = "sub"
        if self._config.output_format in ("md", "html"):
            fmt = self._config.output_format
            logger.warning(
                f"Format {fmt} is deprecated as a data format, "
                f"use '-f tsv --export {fmt}'; writing both"
            )
            self._config.output_format = "tsv"
            self._config.export = fmt
        if self._config.export and not self._config.output_format:
            raise ValueError("An export requires a data format (output_format)")

    @property
    def config(self) -> QueryRunnerConfig:
        return self._config

    def run(self, query_files: Iterable[str]) -> list[list["KmindexQueryResult"]]:
        """Run queries for all provided input paths.

        Args:
            query_files: Paths to FASTA/FASTQ files or directories.  Pass
                ``"-"`` to read from stdin.

        Returns:
            A list of per-query result lists, in the same order as the resolved
            input files (one entry per executed query).
        """
        os.makedirs(self._config.output_dir, exist_ok=True)

        all_results: list[list[KmindexQueryResult]] = []

        resolved, temp_files = self._resolve_files(query_files)
        errors: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        try:

            if self._config.batch:
                batch_path = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "kmhelpers_batch.fa")
                temp_files.append(batch_path)
                with open(batch_path, "wb") as fout:
                    for qfile in resolved:
                        last = b"\n"
                        with open_decompressed(qfile) as fin:
                            while chunk := fin.read(1 << 20):
                                fout.write(chunk)
                                last = chunk[-1:]
                        if last != b"\n":
                            fout.write(b"\n")
                logger.info(f"Batching {len(resolved)} file(s) into a single query...")
                label = f"batch of {len(resolved)} file(s)"
                result, reason = self._run_single_safe(batch_path, 1, 1, label)
                if reason is None:
                    all_results.append(result)
                else:
                    errors.append((label, reason))
            else:
                total = len(resolved)
                for idx, qfile in enumerate(resolved, 1):
                    label = os.path.basename(qfile)
                    result, reason = self._run_single_safe(qfile, total, idx, label)
                    if reason is None:
                        all_results.append(result)
                    else:
                        errors.append((label, reason))
        finally:
            self._remove_temp(temp_files)

        if errors:
            lines = [f"  {label}: {reason}" for label, reason in errors]
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"{len(errors)} query file(s) failed:\n" + "\n".join(lines)
            )

        return all_results

    # ---
    # PRIVATE METHODS

    def _resolve_files(self, query_files: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
        found: list[str] = []
        temp_files: list[str] = []
        for qfile in query_files:
            if qfile == "-":
                data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
                suffix = ".fa" + detect_compression(data[:6])
                tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
                    mode="wb", suffix=suffix, delete=False
                )
                tmp.write(data)
                tmp.close()
                found.append(tmp.name)
                temp_files.append(tmp.name)
            elif os.path.isdir(qfile):
                for root, _, files in os.walk(qfile):
                    for fname in sorted(files):
                        if fname.endswith(DATA_EXT_ALL):
                            found.append(os.path.join(root, fname))
            else:
                if not os.path.isfile(qfile):
                    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Query file not found: {qfile}")
                found.append(qfile)

        resolved: list[str] = []
        try:
            for qfile in found:
                if qfile.endswith(_KMINDEX_UNREADABLE):
                    # Own temp dir keeps the base name, hence the output dir name
                    tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
                    temp_files.append(tmp_dir)
                    name = os.path.basename(qfile)
                    plain = os.path.join(tmp_dir, name[: name.rfind(".")])
                    with open_decompressed(qfile) as fin, open(plain, "wb") as fout:
                        shutil.copyfileobj(fin, fout)
                    qfile = plain
                resolved.append(qfile)
        except Exception:
            self._remove_temp(temp_files)
            raise
        return resolved, temp_files

    @staticmethod
    def _remove_temp(paths: list[str]) -> None:
        for path in paths:
            if os.path.isdir(path):
                shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)
            elif os.path.exists(path):
                os.unlink(path)

    def _run_single_safe(
        self, qfile: str, total: int, idx: int, label: str
    ) -> tuple[list["KmindexQueryResult"], Optional[str]]:
        """Run one query, return (results, None) or ([], failure reason)."""
        self._info_path = None
        try:
            return self._run_single(qfile, total=total, idx=idx), None
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"[{label}] {e}")
            logger.debug(f"[{label}] traceback:", exc_info=True)
            reason = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
            if self._info_path and os.path.isfile(self._info_path):
                reason += f" - see {self._info_path}"
            return [], reason

    def _run_single(
        self, qfile: str, total: int, idx: int
    ) -> list["KmindexQueryResult"]:
        start = time.time()
        cfg = self._config

        stem = strip_data_ext(os.path.basename(qfile))
        query_output = os.path.join(cfg.output_dir, stem)

        if cfg.timestamp:
            query_output = f"{query_output}_{time.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"

        resolved = self._resolve_existing(query_output, stem)
        if resolved is None:
            return []
        query_output = resolved

        logger.info(f"[{idx}/{total}] Querying: {stem}...")

        self._info_path = os.path.join(query_output, "info.yaml")
        kq = KmindexQuery(path=qfile)
        results = kq.execute(
            registry_path=cfg.registry_path,
            output_dir=query_output,
            index_ids=cfg.index_ids,
            z=cfg.zvalue,
            single_query=cfg.single_query,
            aggregate=cfg.aggregate,
            threads=cfg.threads,
            is_compressed=cfg.compressed,
            fast=not cfg.compressed,
            threshold=cfg.threshold,
            method=cfg.parallel,
            vec=cfg.vec,
            keep_query=cfg.keep_query,
        )

        elapsed = time.time() - start
        result_dir = os.path.join(query_output, KMINDEX_QUERY_OUTPUT)
        logger.debug(f"kmindex output dir: {result_dir}")
        logger.info(f"Time: {elapsed:.2f}s")

        self._convert_results(result_dir, kq.info)

        if cfg.on_result is not None:
            cfg.on_result(results)

        return results

    def _registry_info(self) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict]:
        """Samples per queried subindex and run info from the registry,
        both empty if the registry is unreadable."""
        try:
            with open(get_json_path(self._config.registry_path)) as f:
                registry = json.load(f)["index"]
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as e:
            logger.warning(f"Cannot read subindex sizes from the registry: {e}")
            return {}, {}
        names = [n for n in self._config.index_ids or list(registry) if n in registry]
        versions = sorted({str(registry[n].get("kmindex_version", "")) for n in names})
        info = {
            "registry": os.path.abspath(self._config.registry_path),
            "subindexes": ", ".join(names),
            "kmindex_version": ", ".join(v for v in versions if v),
        }
        return {n: registry[n]["nb_samples"] for n in names}, info

    def _resolve_existing(self, output_path: str, label: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return the (possibly adjusted) output path, or ``None`` to skip."""
        if not os.path.exists(output_path):
            return output_path

        strategy = self._config.on_existing

        if strategy == "skip":
            logger.warning(f"Skipping {label}: output directory already exists")
            return None
        elif strategy == "fail":
            raise FileExistsError(f"Output directory already exists: {output_path}")
        elif strategy == "delete":
            if not self._config.force:
                raise PermissionError(
                    f"Output directory exists and force=False: {output_path}. "
                    "Set force=True to delete automatically."
                )
            logger.debug(f"Deleting existing output directory: {output_path}")
            shutil.rmtree(output_path)
            return output_path
        elif strategy == "new-name":
            new_path = f"{output_path}_{time.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
            logger.debug(f"Output directory renamed to: {new_path}")
            return new_path

        return output_path

    def _convert_results(self, result_dir: str, info: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        fmt = self._config.output_format
        out_file = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(result_dir), f"results.{fmt}")
        threshold = self._config.threshold
        sizes, registry_info = self._registry_info()
        metadata = {**(info or {}), **registry_info, "zvalue": self._config.zvalue}
        merged = KmindexQueryResult(metadata=metadata, index_sizes=sizes)
        files = list_result_files(result_dir)
        for json_path in files:
            try:
                merged.load_jsonl(json_path)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to read {json_path}: {e}")

        # Written even without match, the zero counts are informative
        if files and self._config.stats and not self._config.print_output:
            out_dir = os.path.dirname(result_dir)
            for name, content in (
                ("sequence_stats.tsv", merged.generate_sequence_stats_tsv(threshold)),
                ("sample_stats.tsv", merged.generate_sample_stats_tsv(threshold)),
            ):
                with open(os.path.join(out_dir, name), "w") as f:
                    f.write(content)
            logger.info(
                f"Statistics: {os.path.join(out_dir, 'sequence_stats.tsv')}, "
                "sample_stats.tsv"
            )

        if not merged.items and files:
            logger.info(
                f"No match above threshold {threshold} "
                f"({len(files)} result file(s) read)"
            )

        # Reports also list sequences without match, data formats need one
        if self._config.export and files:
            self._write_report(merged, os.path.dirname(result_dir))
        if not fmt or not merged.items:
            return
        converted = merged.convert(format=fmt, threshold=threshold)
        if self._config.print_output:
            sys.stdout.write(f"{converted}\n")
        else:
            with open(out_file, "w") as f:
                f.write(converted)
            logger.info(f"Results: {out_file}")

        # Other formats embed coverage, a matrix TSV cannot hold a second table
        if fmt == "tsv" and merged.has_vectors:
            coverage = merged.generate_coverage_tsv(threshold)
            if self._config.print_output:
                sys.stdout.write(f"{coverage}\n")
            else:
                coverage_file = os.path.join(
                    os.path.dirname(result_dir), "coverage.tsv"
                )
                with open(coverage_file, "w") as f:
                    f.write(coverage)
                logger.info(f"Coverage: {coverage_file}")

    def _write_report(self, merged: "KmindexQueryResult", out_dir: str) -> None:
        cfg = self._config
        assert cfg.export is not None
        files = merged.generate_report(
            cfg.export, cfg.threshold, page_size=cfg.page_size, top=cfg.top
        )
        for rel_path, content in files.items():
            path = os.path.join(out_dir, rel_path)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
            with open(path, "w") as f:
                f.write(content)
        main = next(iter(files))
        detail = f" (+ {len(files) - 1} detail page(s))" if len(files) > 1 else ""
        logger.info(f"Report: {os.path.join(out_dir, main)}{detail}")

def list_result_files(result_dir: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the kmindex result files (JSON lines) found in result_dir.

    A single batch is written as <index>.jsonl at the top level. Several
    batches go to batch_N/<index>.json[l], kmindex only merges them with
    --aggregate, in which case the top-level files are used.
    """

    def scan(path: str) -> list[str]:
        return sorted(
            e.path
            for e in os.scandir(path)
            if e.is_file() and e.name.endswith((".jsonl", ".json"))
        )

    top = scan(result_dir)
    if top:
        return top
    files: list[str] = []
    for e in sorted(os.scandir(result_dir), key=lambda e: e.name):
        if e.is_dir() and e.name.startswith("batch_"):
            files.extend(scan(e.path))
    return files

class QueryReport:
    """md or html report of a KmindexQueryResult."""

    # Sequential blue ramp, light (score 0) to dark (score 1)
    _SCORE_RAMP = (
        "#cde2fb",
        "#9ec5f4",
        "#6da7ec",
        "#3987e5",
        "#256abf",
        "#184f95",
        "#0d366b",
    )
    # From this step on, the background is dark enough to need light text
    _SCORE_RAMP_INVERT = 4
    # Coverage track: bucket count (html), character count (markdown),
    # and color of a fully absent bucket
    _TRACK_BUCKETS = 200
    _TRACK_TEXT_WIDTH = 120
    _TRACK_EMPTY = "#eeeeee"

    # Run info fields kept in reports, in display order
    _RUN_FIELDS: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
        ("date", "Date"),
        ("execution_time_s", "Runtime (s)"),
        ("max_cpu_percent", "Max CPU (%)"),
        ("max_memory_mb", "Max memory (MB)"),
        ("kmindex_version", "kmindex version"),
        ("registry", "Registry"),
        ("subindexes", "Subindexes"),
        ("samples", "Samples"),
        ("threshold", "Threshold"),
        ("zvalue", "z"),
        ("query_file", "Query file"),
        ("command", "Command"),
    )

    def __init__(self, result) -> None:
        self._result = result

    @staticmethod
    def _track_buckets(vector: list[int], width: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, float]]:
        # Downsample a presence vector to (start, end, mean) buckets
        n = len(vector)
        buckets = min(n, width)
        out = []
        for i in range(buckets):
            lo = i * n // buckets
            hi = max((i + 1) * n // buckets, lo + 1)
            chunk = vector[lo:hi]
            out.append((lo, hi, sum(chunk) / len(chunk)))
        return out

    @classmethod
    def _track_text(cls, vector: list[int]) -> str:
        # ASCII coverage track: + all found, ~ partial, - absent
        return "".join(
            "+" if mean == 1 else "-" if mean == 0 else "~"
            for _, _, mean in cls._track_buckets(vector, cls._TRACK_TEXT_WIDTH)
        )

    def _metadata_rows(self, threshold: float) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        # Only the fields actually reported, dry runs carry the command alone
        meta = dict(self._result.metadata)
        if meta.get("start_time") is not None:
            meta["date"] = time.strftime(
                "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", time.localtime(meta["start_time"])
            )
        meta["threshold"] = threshold
        meta["samples"] = self._result.total_samples()
        if not meta.get("subindexes"):
            meta["subindexes"] = ", ".join(
                sorted(self._result.index_sizes or self._result.items)
            )
        return [
            (label, str(meta[key]))
            for key, label in self._RUN_FIELDS
            if meta.get(key) not in (None, "")
        ]

    @classmethod
    def _score_style(cls, score: float) -> str:
        # Map a 0..1 score onto a ramp step, plus a readable text color
        ramp = cls._SCORE_RAMP
        step = min(int(max(score, 0.0) * len(ramp)), len(ramp) - 1)
        fg = "#ffffff" if step >= cls._SCORE_RAMP_INVERT else "#0b0b0b"
        return f"background-color: {ramp[step]}; color: {fg}"

    @classmethod
    def _track_html(cls, vector: list[int]) -> str:
        # Presence vector downsampled to fixed-width buckets, colored by bucket mean
        cells = []
        for lo, hi, mean in cls._track_buckets(vector, cls._TRACK_BUCKETS):
            style = (
                f"background-color: {cls._TRACK_EMPTY}"
                if mean == 0
                else cls._score_style(mean)
            )
            cells.append(f"<span style='{style}' title='{lo}-{hi}: {mean:.2f}'></span>")
        return f"<div class='track'>{''.join(cells)}</div>"

    _REPORT_TITLE = "kmindex query results"

    # Index and overall columns: stats key, label
    _REPORT_COLUMNS: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
        ("samples", "Samples"),
        ("perfect", "Perfect"),
        ("perfect_pct", "Perfect %"),
        ("mean", "Mean"),
        ("median", "Median"),
    )

    @staticmethod
    def _how_to_read(threshold: float, top: int, paged: bool) -> list[str]:
        where = "in the pages of `details/`" if paged else "below the sequence table"
        return [
            "Score: share of the query k-mers found in the sample, from 0 to 1.",
            f"A sample matches a sequence when its score is >= {threshold}. "
            "A perfect match has a score of 1.",
            "Samples: number of matching samples. Perfect % is relative to them, "
            "mean and median are computed over them.",
            "Overall: each sample counts once, with its best score over all sequences.",
            "Sequences: one line per query sequence, the name links to its details. "
            "Sequences without any match have no details.",
            f"Details ({where}): the {top} best samples of each sequence, by score.",
            "Full data: kmindex_output/ (raw JSON lines), sequence_stats.tsv and "
            "sample_stats.tsv (statistics, unless --no-stats).",
        ]

    def _score_cell(self, w: _ReportWriter, score: float) -> str:
        if w.ext == "html":
            style = self._score_style(score)
            return f"<span class='score' style='{style}'>{score:.3f}</span>"
        return f"{score:.3f}"

    def _track_cell(self, w: _ReportWriter, vector: Optional[list[int]]) -> str:
        if not vector:
            return ""
        return (
            self._track_html(vector)
            if w.ext == "html"
            else w.code(self._track_text(vector))
        )

    def _detail_section(
        self, w: _ReportWriter, query: str, anchor: str, hits: dict, top: int
    ) -> str:
        shown = heapq.nlargest(top, hits.items(), key=lambda item: item[1][0])
        with_track = any(vector for _, (_, vector) in shown)
        headers = ["Sample", "Score"] + (["Coverage"] if with_track else [])
        rows = []
        for sample, (score, vector) in shown:
            row = [w.text(sample), self._score_cell(w, score)]
            if with_track:
                row.append(self._track_cell(w, vector))
            rows.append(row)
        parts = [w.heading(2, w.text(query), anchor)]
        if len(hits) > len(shown):
            parts.append(
                w.para(
                    f"{len(shown)} of {len(hits)} matching samples shown, "
                    f"all matches are in kmindex_output/."
                )
            )
        parts.append(w.table(headers, rows))
        return "\n".join(parts)

    def files(
        self,
        fmt: str,
        threshold: float = 0.0,
        page_size: int = 0,
        top: int = 100,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Build a md or html report as {relative path: content}.

        Up to page_size sequences (or page_size 0): a single results.<fmt>.
        More: README.md or index.html, plus details/page_NNN.<fmt> holding
        page_size sequences each. Only the top best samples are listed per
        sequence, statistics use all matches.
        """
        w = _ReportWriter.create(fmt)
        hits = self._result._query_hits(threshold)
        stats = self._result.match_stats(threshold)
        overall = stats.pop()
        queries = [row["query"] for row in stats]
        paged = 0 < page_size < len(queries)
        n_pages = -(-len(queries) // page_size) if paged else 1
        digits = max(3, len(str(n_pages)))

        def page_path(page: int) -> str:
            return f"details/page_{page:0{digits}d}.{w.ext}"

        # Anchors and detail pages, only for sequences with a match
        used: set[str] = set()
        anchors: dict[str, str] = {}
        pages: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
        for pos, query in enumerate(queries):
            if not hits.get(query):
                continue
            anchors[query] = _slug(query, used)
            page = pos // page_size + 1 if paged else 0
            pages.setdefault(page, []).append(
                self._detail_section(w, query, anchors[query], hits[query], top)
            )

        keys = [key for key, _ in self._REPORT_COLUMNS]
        labels = [label for _, label in self._REPORT_COLUMNS]
        index_rows = []
        for pos, row in enumerate(stats):
            query = row["query"]
            name = w.text(query)
            if query in anchors:
                href = f"#{anchors[query]}"
                if paged:
                    href = f"{page_path(pos // page_size + 1)}{href}"
                name = w.link(name, href)
            cells = self._result._stats_cells(row, tuple(keys))
            index_rows.append([name] + [w.text(c) for c in cells])

        overall_cells = self._result._stats_cells(overall, tuple(keys))
        parts = [
            w.heading(2, "Run"),
            w.items(
                [
                    f"{label}: {w.code(value) if label == 'Command' else w.text(value)}"
                    for label, value in self._metadata_rows(threshold)
                ]
            ),
            w.heading(2, "Overall"),
            w.table(labels, [[w.text(c) for c in overall_cells]]),
            w.heading(2, "How to read"),
            w.items(self._how_to_read(threshold, top, paged)),
            w.heading(2, f"Sequences ({len(queries)})"),
            w.table(["Sequence"] + labels, index_rows),
        ]
        if not paged:
            parts.extend(pages.get(0, []))
            return {f"results.{w.ext}": w.page(self._REPORT_TITLE, parts)}

        files = {w.index_name: w.page(self._REPORT_TITLE, parts)}
        for page, sections in pages.items():
            first = (page - 1) * page_size + 1
            last = min(page * page_size, len(queries))
            title = f"{self._REPORT_TITLE}, sequences {first} to {last}"
            back = w.para(w.link("Back to the index", f"../{w.index_name}"))
            files[page_path(page)] = w.page(title, [back] + sections)
        return files

def query_names(self) -> list[str]:
    """All queries seen, including those without any match, in natural

def total_samples(self) -> Optional[int]:
    """Samples in the queried subindexes, None if any size is unknown."""
    sizes = self._index_sizes
    indexes = set(sizes) | set(self._items)
    if indexes and all(i in sizes for i in indexes):
        return sum(sizes[i] for i in indexes)
    return None

def match_stats(self, threshold: float = 0.0) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per query over the whole index, then a "*" row over all
    queries, where each sample counts once with its best score."""
    hits = self._query_hits(threshold)
    rows = []
    best: dict[str, float] = {}
    for query in self.query_names():
        scores = {s: v[0] for s, v in hits.get(query, {}).items()}
        summary = self._score_summary(list(scores.values()))
        rows.append({"query": query, "samples": len(scores), **summary})
        for sample, score in scores.items():
            best[sample] = max(best.get(sample, 0.0), score)
    summary = self._score_summary(list(best.values()))
    rows.append({"query": "*", "samples": len(best), **summary})
    return rows

def sample_stats(self, threshold: float = 0.0) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per matched sample over all queries, then a "*" row where
    each query counts once with its best score over samples. Unmatched
    samples are left out, an index can hold millions of them."""
    by_sample: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    best: dict[str, float] = {}
    for query, samples in self._query_hits(threshold).items():
        for sample, (score, _) in samples.items():
            by_sample.setdefault(sample, []).append(score)
            best[query] = max(best.get(query, 0.0), score)
    rows = [
        {
            "sample": sample,
            "queries": len(by_sample[sample]),
            **self._score_summary(by_sample[sample]),
        }
        for sample in sorted(by_sample, key=_natural_key)
    ]
    summary = self._score_summary(list(best.values()))
    rows.append({"sample": "*", "queries": len(best), **summary})
    return rows

class SpanProfiler:
    """Read a JSONL sample index and write a Bloom-filter span distribution.

    Reads the header line for ``k`` (and optionally ``false_positive_rate``),
    then iterates over sample entries to assign each to a Bloom-filter span
    based on its k-mer count.  Outputs a ``baseline.csv`` and, when
    the plot module is available, a ``profile.yaml`` alongside the
    ``groups.png`` analysis plot.

    Args:
        input_file:          Path to the JSONL sample index (produced by ``list``).
        output_dir:          Directory where output files are written.
        false_positive_rate: Bloom filter false-positive rate (default 0.25).
        n_groups:            Number of storage-balanced span groups. 0 (default)
                             chooses it, see ``SpanAnalyzer.auto_groups``.
        auto_group_samples:  With ``n_groups=0``, about one group per this many
                             samples.
        auto_group_max:      With ``n_groups=0``, the most groups chosen.
        auto_group_min_gain: With ``n_groups=0``, the storage fraction a group
                             must save to be added.
        auto_group_single_max: With ``n_groups=0``, one group when it takes at
                             most this many bytes (presence/absence); None or
                             0: no such size.
        no_grouping:         One group, no grouping strategy (``--no-grouping``).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        input_file: str,
        output_dir: str,
        false_positive_rate: float = 0.25,
        n_groups: int = 0,
        base: float = 2.0,
        auto_group_samples: int = AUTO_GROUP_SAMPLES,
        auto_group_max: int = AUTO_GROUP_MAX,
        auto_group_min_gain: float = AUTO_GROUP_MIN_GAIN,
        auto_group_single_max: int | None = None,
        no_grouping: bool = False,
    ):
        if no_grouping and n_groups:
            raise ValueError("--no-grouping and -g N both set the groups: use one")
        self.input_file = input_file
        self.output_dir = output_dir
        self.false_positive_rate = false_positive_rate
        self.n_groups = n_groups
        self.base = base
        self.auto_group = {
            "samples": auto_group_samples,
            "max": auto_group_max,
            "min_gain": auto_group_min_gain,
            "single_max": auto_group_single_max or None,
        }
        self.no_grouping = no_grouping

    def run(self) -> None:
        with open(self.input_file) as f:
            try:
                header = json.loads(f.readline())
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
                raise ValueError(f"Could not parse header line: {self.input_file}")

            k = header.get("k")
            if not k:
                raise ValueError(f"Key 'k' not found or 0 in header: {self.input_file}")

            sm = SpanManager(p=self.false_positive_rate, b=self.base)
            spans: dict[int, int] = {}
            biggest_sample: tuple[str, int] = ("", 0)
            sample_count = 0

            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    entry = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    logger.warning(f"Could not parse entry: {line}")
                    continue

                name = entry.get("name")
                if not name:
                    continue

                sample_count += 1
                try:
                    logger.debug(f"Process {name}...")
                    kmer_count = entry.get("kmer_count", 0)
                    if kmer_count:
                        s = sm.dispatch(kmer_count)
                        spans[s] = spans.get(s, 0) + 1
                        if kmer_count > biggest_sample[1]:
                            biggest_sample = (name, kmer_count)
                    else:
                        logger.warning(f"{name}: no field 'kmer_count'... skip")
                except Exception as e:
                    Log.handle_exception(
                        logger,
                        e,
                        f"Could not process sample '{name}'",
                        level=logging.WARNING,
                    )

        if not spans:
            raise ValueError(
                f"No samples with k-mer counts found in: {self.input_file}"
            )

        os.makedirs(self.output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        distribution_file = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "baseline.csv")
        with open(distribution_file, "w") as f:
            f.write("span,bf_size,sample_count\n")
            for span_id, count in sorted(spans.items()):
                f.write(f"{span_id},{sm.get_bf_size(span_id)},{count}\n")

        baseline = sorted(spans.keys())

        sa = pykmhelpers.pipeline.span_analyzer.SpanAnalyzer(distribution_file)

        auto_group = None
        if self.no_grouping:
            n_groups = 1
            logger.info("No grouping: one group")
        elif self.n_groups == 0:
            g = self.auto_group
            single = sa.single_group_size()
            n_groups = sa.auto_groups(
                g["samples"], g["max"], g["min_gain"], g["single_max"]
            )
            # Recorded in profile.yaml, so the grouping can be reproduced
            auto_group = dict(g, single_size=single, groups=n_groups)
            if g["single_max"] and single <= g["single_max"]:
                logger.info(
                    f"Auto groups: 1 (one group takes {_size(single)}, "
                    f"at most {_size(g['single_max'])})"
                )
            else:
                logger.info(
                    f"Auto groups: {n_groups} ({sample_count} samples, "
                    f"start {sa.auto_group_start(g['samples'], g['max'])}, "
                    f"max {sa.auto_group_limit(g['max'])}, min gain {g['min_gain']:.0%})"
                )
        else:
            n_groups = min(self.n_groups, len(spans))

        sa.plot(n_groups=n_groups)

        with open(os.path.join(self.output_dir, "profile.yaml"), "w") as f:
            yaml.dump(
                {
                    "false_positive_rate": self.false_positive_rate,
                    "span_base": self.base,
                    "sample_count": sample_count,
                    "biggest_sample": str(biggest_sample),
                    "max_kmer_count": sm.max_kmer_count(baseline[-1]),
                    **({"auto_group": auto_group} if auto_group else {}),
                    **({"grouping": "none"} if self.no_grouping else {}),
                    "default_profile": sa.default_profile or "baseline",
                    "profiles": sa.serialize_profiles(),
                },
                f,
                default_flow_style=False,
                sort_keys=False,
            )

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: kmhelpers commands cover the full k-mer index lifecycle: build indices from raw sequences, then query them. The terms used here (shard, partition, session, chunk...) are defined in the Glossary. Most workflows only need three top-level commands - design, build, and query. Click on any command below to see its full options, inputs/outputs, examples, and additional information.

docs.title: Main Pipeline
docs.text: Command Description design Discover samples, profile them, and compose index definitions (steps: list → profile → compose) build Plan then build indices (steps: plan → apply) query Query indices with FASTA/FASTQ sequences compress Compress the shards of a registry (under development)

docs.title: Design (manual steps)
docs.text:
Steps run internally by design:

Command Description list Step 1 - scan a directory and count k-mers profile Step 2 - compute Bloom-filter distribution compose Step 3 - generate index definition files

docs.title: Build (manual steps)
docs.text:
Steps run internally by build:

Command Description plan Step 1 - validate paths, decide the whole build and write the plan (scripts, jobs, SLURM files) apply Step 2 - run the plan: build, merge and register the indices

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text: Command Description manage Manage k-mer index registries (under development) pipeline Run a sequence of commands defined in a YAML pipeline file check-deps Check that kmindex, kmtricks and ntcard are callable install-deps Download and install kmtricks, kmindex and ntcard prebuilt binaries

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
These options are available on the root kmhelpers command and apply to all subcommands:

-C, --config FILE         YAML config file for default values  [env var:
                          KMHELPERS_CONFIG]
-V, --verbose             Increase verbosity: -V for DEBUG
-Q, --quiet               Decrease verbosity: -Q for WARNING, -QQ for ERROR,
                          -QQQ for CRITICAL
--NF, --no-log-formatting  Disable log formatter  [env var:
                          KMHELPERS_NO_LOG_FORMATTING]
-L, --log-file FILE       Path to log file (logs will be written in addition
                          to console output)  [env var: KMHELPERS_LOG_FILE]
--chdir DIRECTORY         Change to directory before initialization  [env
                          var: KMHELPERS_RUN_DIR]
-Y, --yes                 Automatically answer yes to all confirmation
                          prompts.  [env var: KMHELPERS_SKIP_CONFIRMATION]

Also honors KMHELPERS_LOG_LEVEL: default log level 0-4 (0=CRITICAL, 4=DEBUG) before -V/-Q adjustments. Default: 3 (INFO).

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
-C, --config FILE (or KMHELPERS_CONFIG=FILE) reads default option values from a YAML file, for every command:

# kmhelpers.yaml
limits: '{"ram": 120000000000, "threads": 24}'
chunks_per_job: 4
false_positive_rate: 0.25
auto_group_min_gain: 0.25

kmhelpers -C kmhelpers.yaml plan coli_db -o coli_build/
export KMHELPERS_CONFIG=$PWD/kmhelpers.yaml      # same, for every command

  • Keys are the parameter names: the long option name with _ for - (--chunks-per-job → chunks_per_job). A dashed key (chunks-per-job) is ignored without warning. A few options have another parameter name:

    Option Key Commands -o, --output-dir work_dir plan, apply, build -o, --output output_dir (profile), output_file (list) -s, --session session_id design, compose (session in plan, apply, build) --sh, --shard index_ids plan, query, compress --task task_ids apply -g, --group n_groups design, profile --ab, --abundance-bits bitw design, compose --cluster cluster_file plan -x, --fail-fast fail_on_error plan, apply -p, --paired pair_regex design, list --continue do_continue list

  • One flat mapping for all commands: a key applies to every command that has this parameter (e.g. threads), and is ignored by the others. Options of manage subcommands are not read from it.

  • Precedence: see below. A config file therefore sets the defaults of a site or a project, and any command can still override them.
  • Values are typed as on the command line: JSON options such as limits are strings, flags are true/false.
  • pipeline uses the same file as the base of every step, below the step's own values and -x KEY VALUE.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Sets Commands KMHELPERS_CONFIG -C, --config: the configuration file above all KMHELPERS_LOG_LEVEL default log level 0-4 (0=CRITICAL, 4=DEBUG, default 3=INFO), before -V/-Q all KMHELPERS_LOG_FILE -L, --log-file all KMHELPERS_NO_LOG_FORMATTING --NF, --no-log-formatting all KMHELPERS_RUN_DIR --chdir: directory to work in all KMHELPERS_SKIP_CONFIRMATION -Y, --yes: answer yes to every confirmation all KMHELPERS_SEED seed of the random generator, for reproducible test data test KMHELPERS_AUTO_GROUP_SAMPLES --auto-group-samples (default 1000) profile, design KMHELPERS_AUTO_GROUP_MAX --auto-group-max (default 20) profile, design KMHELPERS_AUTO_GROUP_MIN_GAIN --auto-group-min-gain (default 0.2) profile, design KMHELPERS_AUTO_GROUP_SINGLE_MAX --auto-group-single-max (profile: none; design: 4GB of built index) profile, design KMINDEX_BIN_PATH, KMTRICKS_BIN_PATH, NTCARD_BIN_PATH directory of the tool, put first on PATH (see check-deps) all that run the tool

design hides the --auto-group-* options: set them with their variables, or in the configuration file. --help lists the variable of each option ([env var: ...]).

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
When an option is set in several places, the first one found wins:

  1. the command line (--chunks-per-job 0);
  2. the environment variable of the option (KMHELPERS_AUTO_GROUP_MIN_GAIN=0.3);
  3. the configuration file (-C, KMHELPERS_CONFIG);
  4. the default of the option (as shown by --help).

For example, with auto_group_min_gain: 0.5 in the configuration file, KMHELPERS_AUTO_GROUP_MIN_GAIN=0.3 kmhelpers -C kmhelpers.yaml profile ... uses 0.3, and profile --auto-group-min-gain 0.1 uses 0.1 whatever the variable and the file say.

docs.title: Option names
docs.text:
• Global options, given before the command, have uppercase short flags (-V, -Q, -Y, -C, -L).
  • Command options are lowercase. When a letter is already taken in a command, the option gets a short double-dash name instead (query --thr, --threshold, plan --off, --offline).
  • Long names never change.
  • Every command takes -h, --help, and -H, --HELP to also list its hidden (expert) options.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Run the plan written by plan: build, merge and register the indices.

USAGE

kmhelpers apply [OPTIONS] INPUT
Argument Description INPUT The INPUT given to plan: the design directory, a compose directory or one of its indexes, a session or its index.yaml, or one shard file (required) -s, --session SESSION Session to use when INPUT is a directory (default: the last one composed) -o, --output-dir BUILD_DIR The BUILD_DIR given to plan (required)

I/O

Input: BUILD_DIR/assets/SESSION/plan.yaml, written by plan for the same INPUT and BUILD_DIR Output: indices in BUILD_DIR/<name>/, registered in BUILD_DIR/index.json

See build - Paths for the directory layout.

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text:
Option Description --task TEXT Run only what matches these names or glob patterns (repeatable or comma-separated): a shard (idx_g0) or its task (idx_g0_initial) runs all its jobs; a job runs alone, <shard>_j<k> (some of its chunks) or <shard>_merge (see plan - Jobs and Selecting what runs) --pending Print the jobs not done yet, one per line, and run nothing --status Print the status of every step, per shard, write it to progress.yaml, and run nothing; with --notify, mail it (see Progress) --sp, --show-progress One line per shard: progress bar of its steps, steps running, colored end status (see Following a build); with --status, follow a cluster build until it ends --interval SECONDS With --status --sp: seconds between two reads of a cluster build (default: 30) -x, --fail-fast Abort on first failure instead of going on with the other shards --notify EMAIL Send email notifications (requires sendmail), with the progress, the log and the apply report attached --notify-level global\|shard global (default): one mail at the end; shard: also one mail per shard when it ends (see build - Notifications)

apply takes no sizing option (--limits, --chunk-budget, ...): they are decisions of the plan.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
apply loads the plan and refuses it when it is stale: an input file changed since plan (definition, shard files, layout.yaml, sample lists, --cluster file), or another kmhelpers version made it. Run plan again then.

Then it runs the selected jobs (all by default), in order. Each step is checked before it runs, so a job can be run again after an interruption, or by several processes in turn:

  • a shard is done when it is registered and holds every sample of the plan's chunks: its jobs do nothing;
  • a chunk is skipped when its kmtricks run is complete (reused), else its script deletes what an earlier attempt left and builds it;
  • a merge needs every chunk of its shard complete; it checks that the registry is as plan saw it (expects), or as an interrupted run of this same merge leaves it, and refuses otherwise.

A failed step stops its shard; the other shards go on, unless --fail-fast. Logs are in BUILD_DIR/logs/<shard>/ (<run>.log with the kmtricks output and its resource use, merge.log).

docs.title: Following a build
docs.text:
--sp, --show-progress draws one line per shard, once its first step has started:

⣾ idx_g0  [■■■■■■      ] 6/11 (8m3s)   8 running: chunk2 (4m10s), chunk5 (3m12s), chunk8 (52s), ...
⣽ idx_g1  [■■■■■■■■■■■ ] 10/11 (12m40s) merge (3m4s)
✔ idx_g2  [■■■■■■■■■■■■] 8/8  (25m14s) SUCCESS
✘ idx_g3  [■■■         ] 3/9  (6m2s)   FAILED chunk3 (log: logs/idx_g3/idx_g3_initial_chunk3.log), 2 still running
  • the bar and the count are the steps of the shard done: its kmtricks runs (chunk<N>, or run when it is built in one run) and its merge; the time is the shard's, since its first step started;
  • several chunks of a shard run at once on a cluster with plan --chunks-per-job N (one per array task): the line shows how many, and the 3 oldest with their time;
  • an ended shard keeps its line: SUCCESS (green), FAILED (red), LOST or CANCELLED (yellow), with the failed step and its log.

In a terminal, the lines are redrawn in place (log lines print above them); otherwise (redirected to a file, a SLURM job), a shard's line is printed each time one of its steps ends.

For a cluster build, apply --status --sp (or build --hpc --sp right after the submission) draws the same lines, read again every --interval seconds, until no shard is running or waiting on a job: it exits 0 when every shard is SUCCESS, 1 otherwise. Ctrl-C stops watching; the jobs go on.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
Each step apply runs is recorded in BUILD_DIR/assets/SESSION/<shard>/state/<step>.json (status, job, node, times, log, error), and BUILD_DIR/assets/SESSION/progress.yaml is rewritten after each one. apply --status prints it, refreshed:

Status Meaning SUCCESS the run is complete, or the shard holds the samples of its task (from the build directory, whatever was recorded) FAILED the step failed: its log and the last line of its error CANCELLED the job got SIGTERM (scancel, time limit) during the step RUNNING started by a job (job, node, start time) LOST recorded as running, but its job is no longer in squeue: it ended without a status (out of memory, node failure); see its SLURM log PENDING not run yet; (job X) when submit.sh submitted it, ended without running it when that job is gone (a step before it failed, or a dependency was cancelled): submit again

--status exits 0 whatever the status; the summary line gives the overall one (SUCCESS, FAILED, RUNNING, PENDING).

Report - BUILD_DIR/logs/kmhelpers_apply_<timestamp>.yaml: per shard, for each kmtricks run whether it was built, reused or already published, its duration, peak RSS, CPU efficiency and share of the RAM limit (from its log); the merge, its duration and size on disk. It is written after each job, with status RUNNING until the end, so a running or killed apply leaves its report so far. See build - Report.

docs.title: Selecting what runs
docs.text:
--task takes names or glob patterns (repeatable or comma-separated). A pattern selects every job whose name, task or shard it matches, so a shard or task name runs all the jobs of that shard, and a job name runs only that job:

--task Runs idx_g0 or idx_g0_initial every job of that shard (shard or task name) 'idx_g0_*' every job of the group-0 shards idx_g0_j1 that one job 'idx_g0_j*' the shard's chunk jobs, not its merge '*_merge' every merge

A pattern that matches nothing is a warning; only no match at all is an error (No task matches ...). Job names are listed in plan.yaml (jobs: of each task), and --pending prints those not done yet.

docs.title: Running jobs separately
docs.text:
With plan --chunks-per-job N, the chunks of a shard are split into jobs that can run at the same time, e.g. as the tasks of a SLURM array, then the merge job of the shard. plan --cluster writes the SLURM files submitting them (see plan - Cluster); by hand:

kmhelpers plan coli_db -o coli_build/ --chunks-per-job 4
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --pending          # the jobs to run
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --task coli_g0_j0  # one per array task
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --task coli_g0_merge

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Run the whole plan
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/

# Run the jobs of some shards
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --task coli_g0,coli_g1
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --task 'coli_g0_*'

# Show progress, abort on first error
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --sp -x

# Notify by email when done
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --notify user@example.com

# Where every shard and step stands
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --status

# Follow a cluster build, one line per shard, until it ends
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --status --sp

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• plan - decide everything and write the plan
  • build - run plan then apply in a single command
  • compose - generate index definition files
  • pipeline - run multiple steps in sequence

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Validate paths then build k-mer indices from an index definition file in a single command.

USAGE

kmhelpers build [OPTIONS] INPUT
Argument Description INPUT The design directory (DESIGN_DIR of design), a compose directory or one of its indexes (COMPOSE_DIR/NAME), a session (COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/SESSION or its index.yaml), or one shard file (SESSION/shards/<shard>.yaml, built without merge) (required) -s, --session SESSION Session to use when INPUT is a directory (default: the last one composed) -o, --output-dir BUILD_DIR Index directory: receives the built index, reused across builds and passed to query -r (required)

I/O

Input: DESIGN_DIR of design (or COMPOSE_DIR of compose), with -s to pick a session; it resolves to compose/NAME/SESSION/index.yaml (see design - Next Step) Output: indices in BUILD_DIR/<name>/, registered in BUILD_DIR/index.json

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text: Option Description --bp, --base-path DIR Base path to resolve relative sample paths --threads INT Hidden. Force the number of kmtricks threads instead of sizing them from --limits --limits JSON Resource limits used to auto-size threads/partitions when --threads is not set (ram, files, threads), and the inputs of one merge (ram, files, maps = vm.max_map_count); see build - Builds and merges --safety-margin FLOAT Fraction of a detected system limit to use for any key missing from --limits (default: 0.9) --max-chunks INT Max number of kmtricks chunks a shard is built in; bigger chunks mean fewer build/merge passes but fewer threads. 0 disables the cap (default: 64) --cb, --chunk-budget INT K-mer budget of one kmtricks chunk: a chunk of span s holds at most ceil8(budget / base^s) samples. 0 for no limit (default: 2**37), see build - Shards and chunks --ncp, --skip-compression Skip compression of intermediate files during index building (useful on slow disks) --keep-previous Keep the replaced version of an updated index in BUILD_DIR/work/SESSION/previous/ instead of deleting it --sp, --show-progress One line per shard: progress bar of its steps, steps running, colored end status (see apply - Following a build); with --hpc, follow the cluster build after the submission --cpj, --chunks-per-job INT Chunks of a shard one job builds (see plan - Jobs) --hpc, --cluster FILE Build on a cluster: plan for the jobs of FILE, submit them, and exit (see On a cluster) --notify EMAIL Send email notifications (requires sendmail), see Notifications --notify-level global\|shard global (default): one mail at the end of the build; shard: also one mail per shard when it ends

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
Two directories are involved, and they are distinct:

  • COMPOSE_DIR holds the index definitions. It is the -o of compose, or DESIGN_DIR/compose/ when using design.
  • BUILD_DIR holds the built index. It is the -o of build, and the -r of query.
coli_db/                          DESIGN_DIR (design -o): INPUT of build
└── compose/                      COMPOSE_DIR
    └── coli/                     NAME: the index
        ├── layout.yaml           state of the index, shared by its sessions
        ├── initial/              SESSION (design/compose -s)
        │   ├── index.yaml        what INPUT resolves to (-s initial)
        │   └── shards/           one definition per shard (coli_g0_p0.yaml, ...)
        └── update/               the last session: built by default
            ├── index.yaml
            └── shards/

coli_build/                       BUILD_DIR (build -o, query -r): the kmindex registry
├── index.json                    registry of all built indices
├── coli_g0_p0/                   an index, in place (a directory, not a symlink)
├── coli_g1_p0/
├── work/                         only while a SESSION is being built
│   └── update/                   SESSION
│       ├── runs/                 kmtricks runs (parts, chunks)
│       ├── merges/               throwaway merge registries and their outputs
│       └── previous/             replaced version of an updated index
├── assets/
│   ├── initial/                  one folder per SESSION
│   │   ├── plan.yaml             the plan, run by apply (see plan)
│   │   ├── slurm/                with plan --cluster
│   │   └── coli_g0_p0/           one folder per shard: <part>[_chunk<N>].sh and .fof, merge.sh, merge/
│   └── update/
└── logs/
    ├── kmhelpers_plan_<timestamp>.yaml    plan report, see Report below
    ├── kmhelpers_apply_<timestamp>.yaml   apply report
    └── coli_g0_p0/                        <run>.log of each kmtricks run, merge.log

Reuse the same BUILD_DIR for every session of an index. Each index keeps one folder, BUILD_DIR/<name>/, for its whole life; a session only uses BUILD_DIR/work/SESSION/ while it is built, and deletes it when it is done. Index names cannot be work, assets, logs, or start with ..

Building a session again resumes it: complete kmtricks runs are kept, incomplete ones are rebuilt, finished merges are not redone, and parts whose samples are already in their index are skipped. A finished session built again changes nothing. A run of <shard>/merge.sh interrupted at any point is finished by running it again (or apply): until the new version of a sub-index is registered, the sub-index is either registered with its previous folder or not registered at all, never registered with other data.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
build chains plan and apply into a single invocation. It is equivalent to running the two commands in sequence.

Step 1 - plan: validates all sample paths upfront, takes every build decision and writes the plan to BUILD_DIR/assets/SESSION/: plan.yaml and one folder of scripts per shard (see plan), and the plan report to BUILD_DIR/logs/. Fix any path errors before the build starts rather than discovering them mid-run.

Step 2 - apply: runs the plan, registers all completed indices in BUILD_DIR/index.json, and writes the apply report as it goes.

Filtering - build always processes every shard of the session. Use plan with --shard (names or glob patterns), then apply (--task), to build a subset or to spread the jobs over several nodes.

docs.title: On a cluster
docs.text:
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/ --hpc cluster.yaml [--chunks-per-job 4] [--notify you@example.com]
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --status          # where it stands, any time
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --status --sp     # one line per shard, until it ends

With --hpc FILE (see plan - Cluster), build plans for the jobs of FILE, runs the generated slurm/submit.sh, and exits: the SLURM jobs build the indices. Nothing is submitted when the plan is FAILED or PARTIAL. The jobs are:

  1. the build array: one task per build job (a shard, or --chunks-per-job chunks of it);
  2. one merge job per shard, after the array tasks of that shard;
  3. a finish job, after every job, successful or not: it checks the registry when everything is built, writes progress.yaml, and sends the final mail.

A failed job cancels the jobs waiting on it (--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes), so the finish job always runs. Run the same build command again (or slurm/submit.sh) to resubmit what is not done: finished work is kept, and a job still queued or running is not submitted twice.

Progress - apply --status prints, per shard, the status of each kmtricks run and merge, and writes it to BUILD_DIR/assets/SESSION/progress.yaml (also rewritten by every job, after each step):

idx_g0:
  idx_g0_initial_chunk0: SUCCESS
  idx_g0_initial_chunk1: FAILED (log: logs/idx_g0/idx_g0_initial_chunk1.log, idx_g0_initial_chunk1.sh failed (exit 1): ...)
  idx_g0_initial_chunk2: RUNNING (job 18001_2, node12, since 10:02)
  idx_g0_initial_chunk3: PENDING (job 18001_3)
  merge: PENDING (job 18002)

See apply - Progress for the statuses.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
--notify EMAIL mails the build's status (requires sendmail, on the compute nodes too for a cluster build), with the progress tree in the body:

--notify-level Mails global (default) one at the end of the build: success, failure, or CANCELLED on SIGTERM shard also one per shard when it ends: published, or failed (the step and its log)

Locally, the mails are sent by the build process, with the log file and the apply report attached. On a cluster, the jobs ending a shard send the shard mails, and the finish job the final one, with progress.yaml attached. SLURM's own mails remain available through extra: in the cluster file (--mail-user, --mail-type).

docs.title: Shards and chunks
docs.text:
A shard is fixed at design: a span is split into shards of at most ceil8(shard_budget / base^s) samples, see compose - Sharding. Each build then splits the new samples of a shard into kmtricks runs (chunks), <part>_chunk<N>. A chunk holds the smallest of:

  1. Open files: files / threads - 1, from --limits files (or the hard open-files limit, ulimit -Hn, x --safety-margin: kmhelpers and its generated scripts raise the soft limit to the hard one before running anything);
  2. Chunk budget: ceil8(chunk_budget / base^s) samples (--chunk-budget, default 2**37, 0 for no limit);
  3. the samples of the part.

--max-chunks (default 64, 0 disables it) then raises the chunk to ceil(samples / max_chunks), so a shard is built in at most that many runs, with fewer threads to stay within the open files. It never goes above bounds 1 and 2: when it would have to, plan warns and uses more chunks. With the default budgets, a full shard fits 64 chunks (2**43 = 64 x 2**37).

docs.title: Builds and merges
docs.text:
Every sub-index is built as unregistered kmtricks runs, then published:

  1. Build - each part of the sub-index (its samples of this session) is built with kmtricks pipeline into BUILD_DIR/work/SESSION/runs/<part>/, not registered. When one kmtricks build cannot hold all the samples of a part (open files, --chunk-budget and --max-chunks, see Shards and chunks), the part is built in chunks, <part>_chunk<N>/. Each run has its script, assets/SESSION/<shard>/<run>.sh, which can be run anywhere, e.g. as a SLURM array task (see plan - Jobs).
  2. Check - assets/SESSION/<shard>/merge.sh starts by checking every run: run_infos.txt (written by kmtricks only when it finishes), kmtricks.fof, options.txt, and all partition matrices present, non-empty and of equal size. If one run is incomplete, the script stops before registering or merging anything; rebuild that run and run the merge script again.
  3. Publish a single run - a new sub-index built in one run is moved in place (kmindex register --mode move): no copy, no merge.
  4. Merge - otherwise the runs, plus the current version of the sub-index when it is already registered (see Updating an index), are merged. Each kmindex merge runs in a throwaway registry, BUILD_DIR/work/SESSION/merges/<name>/<step>/, holding only its inputs. kmindex merge loads the repartition table of every registered sub-index (2 MiB each at minimizer size 10), so a registry limited to the inputs keeps its memory proportional to what is merged. Merges get at most one thread per partition.
  5. Sub-shards - one merge can take at most k inputs: ram / (2 * 4^m) (anonymous memory), (maps - 1000) / threads (vm.max_map_count) and files / threads - 1 (open files), with the values of --limits. More inputs are merged in balanced groups of at most k (<name>__sub1_<i>), then these are merged, and so on. Each level reads and writes the data once more.
  6. Swap - holding the lock BUILD_DIR/.registry.lock (several merge jobs may publish at once): the sub-index is unregistered, its current version is moved to work/SESSION/previous/, the merge result is moved to BUILD_DIR/<name>/, and registered. Queries see the previous version until the swap; during it (a second or so) the sub-index is not queryable. Moves are renames (an internal kmhelpers manage move-dir), so they take the same time whatever the size; they fail instead of copying if work/ is on another filesystem.
  7. Check, then clean up - kmhelpers manage check --shard <name> checks the published sub-index; only then are the runs, merges and previous version deleted. A failed check stops the script with everything kept.

apply runs the run scripts of a shard, then its merge.sh. The plan logs, for each merge, its number of inputs, the limit that sets k, and its expected memory: the anonymous part must fit in RAM, while the mapped inputs are page cache that the kernel reclaims when they exceed it. The same merge plan is in the report, under publish.steps.

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
plan and apply each write a YAML report to BUILD_DIR/logs/: kmhelpers_plan_<timestamp>.yaml and kmhelpers_apply_<timestamp>.yaml (build writes kmhelpers_plan_* and kmhelpers_build_*). Both are organised by shard: plan records what will be built, apply what happened.

  • plan writes its report once done; every run is planned.
  • apply writes it after each job, with summary.status: RUNNING until the end: a running or killed apply leaves its report so far. The --notify mail attaches it.
  • Each kmtricks run that apply runs writes logs/<shard>/<run>.log (command, execution time, max CPU and memory, kmtricks output); the report reads its run metrics from there.
An apply report (abridged)

Reading it

  • A slow run: a cpu_efficiency well below 1 means kmtricks waits on its inputs (slow storage, or a node with a bad mount or network). Compare duration_s and system.host with other runs of similar size.
  • Memory headroom: ram_limit_use is the share of the RAM limit the run used at its peak. Close to 1, lower --safety-margin or --limits ram; far below it on every run, the limit can be raised for more threads.
  • A killed job: a report still RUNNING after the job ended was cut off; it lists the runs done so far. Run apply again: complete runs are reused.
  • Scripts run by hand: a run script run without apply writes no log, so its run has no metrics, also when a later apply reuses it.

docs.title: Updating an index
docs.text:
Building a new SESSION into a BUILD_DIR that already holds the same index adds the new samples to it. kmindex cannot add samples to an existing index in place, so an update merges the current version and the new runs into a new index:

  • The updated index NAME_gN replaces the previous one in BUILD_DIR/NAME_gN/. It keeps its name and its folder, so queries need no change.
  • The previous version is deleted once the updated one is registered and checked. Use --keep-previous to keep it in BUILD_DIR/work/SESSION/previous/NAME_gN/ instead, e.g. to compare both versions; delete that folder once done.
  • Only the sub-indices that receive new samples are merged. The others are untouched.
  • A sample can only be added once: a part whose samples are all already in the index is skipped, and a part where only some are fails.

Disk space

Both versions coexist on disk during the merge. Plan for at least twice the size of the sub-indices being updated.

Indices built by older versions of kmhelpers (registered as symlinks to BUILD_DIR/kmindex_data/SESSION/NAME_gN/) keep working. Updating one moves it in place, and deletes its previous version in kmindex_data/.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Build the index defined by design/compose in session "initial"
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/

# Add an update session to the same index directory
kmhelpers build coli_db -s update -o coli_build/

# Set threads and show progress
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/ --limits '{"threads": 8}' --sp

# Notify by email when done, and at the end of each shard
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/ --notify user@example.com --notify-level shard

# Build on a SLURM cluster, then follow it
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/ --hpc cluster.yaml --notify user@example.com
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --status

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Check that kmindex, kmtricks and ntcard are callable.

USAGE

kmhelpers check-deps

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For each tool, check-deps resolves its path and runs <tool> --version, then logs the version and path. A warning is logged for each tool that cannot be found.

A <TOOL>_BIN_PATH environment variable (e.g. KMINDEX_BIN_PATH) is prepended to PATH before the lookup.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
$ kmhelpers --NF check-deps
INFO     | kmindex    kmindex v0.6.1       /opt/kmhelpers/.env/bin/kmindex
INFO     | kmtricks   kmtricks v1.6.0      /opt/kmhelpers/.env/bin/kmtricks
WARNING  | ntcard     ntcard not found. Either add its installation directory to PATH, or set the NTCARD_BIN_PATH environment variable to that directory.

Missing tools can be installed with install-deps (kmtricks and kmindex only).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Compose index definition file(s) from a sample list produced by list. Building a new index requires a profile from profile.

USAGE

kmhelpers compose -o COMPOSE_DIR -n NAME [--pf PROFILES_FILE] [-s SESSION] [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE
Argument Description INPUT_FILE JSONL sample list produced by list -o, --output-dir COMPOSE_DIR Output directory for index definitions -n, --name TEXT Name of created or updated index --pf, --profiles-file FILE Profiles YAML file with index configuration (required to build a new index) -s, --session SESSION Session name: subdirectory of COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/ and tag appended to index names (default: timestamp)

I/O

Input: JSONL sample list (from list), profiles YAML required only for new index creation (from profile) Output: the session in COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/SESSION/ (index.yaml, samples.jsonl unless --no-copy-list, summary.csv, shards/), and the layout COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/layout.yaml. Pass COMPOSE_DIR (with -s SESSION) to plan, build or apply

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text: Option Description --pr, --profile TEXT Profile name to use (default: default_profile from profiles file) -P, --partition-count INT Hidden. Fix the partition count of every shard for the life of the index: inherited by every later session, no longer adapted to the system limits of plan/build. 0 (default) lets the first plan of each shard size it, see Partitioning below --minim-size INT Minimizer size (4-15), fixed for the life of the index (default: 10 for a new index, the layout's value on an update) --sb, --shard-budget INT Shard budget: a shard of span s holds at most ceil8(budget / base^s) samples (e.g. 2**43); 0 for no limit (default: 2**43 for a new index, the layout's rule on an update) --kr, --kmer-ratio FLOAT Multiply the k-mer ratio (k-mer occurrences per counted k-mer) that sizes the build memory (default: 1), see Partitioning below --ncl, --no-copy-list Point the index definition files to the input sample list instead of copying it into the compose output folder; the list must then stay in place and unchanged as it is used for building --shard-budget-bytes SIZE Hidden. Cap a shard by its size on disk (e.g. 256GB, 500000MB) rather than by --shard-budget: when set, --shard-budget is not used. Cannot be combined with --shard-budget --ab, --abundance-bits INT Build an abundance index with N bits per cell (2^N abundance classes); 0 builds a presence/absence index (default: 0)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Takes a JSONL sample list (produced by list) and generates index definition files that can be passed to plan, build or apply.

Output files are written to COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/SESSION/, where SESSION defaults to the current timestamp if --session is not provided:

  • index.yaml describes the session: parameters, size, and the shards it adds samples to;
  • shards/<shard>.yaml lists the samples of each shard, and samples.jsonl their files; with --no-copy-list, the shards point to the input list instead (sample_file), relative when it lies in the parent of COMPOSE_DIR (e.g. a design's list/), absolute otherwise;
  • summary.csv has one row per shard.

Pass COMPOSE_DIR (or COMPOSE_DIR/NAME, or the session's index.yaml) to plan, build or apply, with -s SESSION to pick a session other than the last one.

Building a new index - provide --profiles-file (produced by profile). A layout file is written to COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/layout.yaml for future updates.

Updating an existing index - omit --profiles-file. The layout file at COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/layout.yaml is detected and loaded automatically.

If --profile is not specified, the default_profile field in the profiles file is used.

Minimizer size - set at design (--minim-size, default 10) and recorded in the layout and in the session's definitions. Indexes can only be merged when they share it, so an update takes the layout's value and refuses another one. plan, apply and build have no --minim-size.

Partitioning - each Bloom filter is split into N partition files, and a shard can only be merged with updates built with the same N. By default compose leaves it open, and plan (or apply/build) chooses it for each shard, in this order:

  1. a shard already built in BUILD_DIR keeps its count, so the session merges into it; any other value is ignored, with a warning;
  2. a part whose kmtricks runs are already started in BUILD_DIR/work/SESSION/ keeps theirs (apply after plan, a resumed build);
  3. the count fixed at design with -P;
  4. otherwise, a count sized from the resource limits (--limits) for a full shard.

plan, apply and build have no -P: they never write the design, and each machine sizes the shards it builds first. Fixing -P at design is inherited by every later session and is no longer adapted to the system limits.

k-mer ratio - kmtricks holds every k-mer occurrence of a sample partition in memory before it filters them (--hard-min), about occurrences / partitions × 8 bytes per thread. The Bloom filter capacity counts distinct k-mers (solid ones for raw reads), so plan sizes partitions and threads from that capacity × the shard's k-mer ratio, recorded as kmer_ratio in index.yaml and in each shard file:

  • per sample, kmer_total / kmer_count from the sample list (list records both), at least 1; without kmer_total, 1 for assembled data and 4 for raw reads;
  • per shard, the largest ratio of its samples, multiplied by --kmer-ratio.

Deep raw reads

Deep raw reads (e.g. metabarcoding) can reach hundreds of occurrences per solid k-mer. For a list without kmer_total, raise --kmer-ratio or fix -P at design.

The layout also records, per span, the samples composed so far (total_samples) and the number of sessions that added samples to it (updates).

Sharding - a span is split into independent shards, instead of one index growing without bound. Shards are never merged together: each one is built and registered on its own, and a query hits them all.

The per-span sample limit of a shard follows one rule:

  • the shard budget (from Logan), on by default: a shard of span s holds at most ceil8(budget / base^s) samples (--shard-budget, default 2**43, about k-mers x samples). --shard-budget 0 disables it;
  • or, with the hidden --shard-budget-bytes SIZE, its size on disk instead: a shard costs about bf_size x samples x bitw / 8 bytes, rounded down to a multiple of 8 samples (minimum 8).

The rule (shard_budget or shard_size) and the shard limit of each span (max_samples) are written to the layout file, together with the shards and their sample counts, so a later session knows where to continue. An update keeps the layout's rule; passing --shard-budget or --shard-budget-bytes again re-shards it, affecting only the shards opened later. Layouts written with the former chunk model read as a shard budget of chunk_budget x shard_chunks.

How a shard is split into kmtricks chunks is decided at build time, see build - Shards and chunks.

An update fills the last shard of the span until that limit is reached, then opens a new one. Filling a shard means merging the session's new samples into it; only chunks (a build-time split, see plan) are merged as well.

Shards are named NAME_g<i>_p<k>. Without any limit (--shard-budget 0), a span keeps a single index named NAME_g<i>.

Abundance - by default an index records the presence or absence of each k-mer in each sample. With --abundance-bits N, each sample gets N bits per Bloom filter cell instead of one, holding the abundance class of the k-mer (2^N classes, kmindex uses 2 by default). The index is then built by kmtricks with --mode hash:bfc:bin --bitw N, takes N times more space, and a query reports the abundance class of each sample instead of the fraction of k-mers found. N is stored in the layout and fixed for the life of the index: an update with another value is refused.

Hard min - k-mers seen fewer times than the abundance_min of the JSONL header are dropped at build time. list sets it to 1 for assembled data and 2 for raw reads.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Build a new index (writes layout to ./db/my_index/layout.yaml)
kmhelpers compose samples.jsonl -o ./db -n my_index --pf profiles.yaml

# Build with a session tag (output goes to ./db/my_index/my_session/)
kmhelpers compose samples.jsonl -o ./db -n my_index --pf profiles.yaml -s my_session

# Use a specific profile
kmhelpers compose samples.jsonl -o ./db -n my_index --pf profiles.yaml --profile baseline

# Fix the partition count of every shard (inherited by later sessions)
kmhelpers compose samples.jsonl -o ./db -n my_index --pf profiles.yaml --partition-count 4

# Split spans into smaller shards
kmhelpers compose samples.jsonl -o ./db -n my_index --pf profiles.yaml --shard-budget 2**40

# Update an existing index (auto-detects ./db/my_index/layout.yaml)
kmhelpers compose samples.jsonl -o ./db -n my_index

docs.text:
