docs.title: Design: plan prepares, apply runs
docs.text: Status: implemented (see commands/plan.md and commands/apply.md for the reference). No backward compatibility is kept.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• plan takes every build decision and writes a runnable bundle.
  • apply only runs and monitors that bundle: it has no sizing option, and cannot run without a plan.
  • What was reviewed in plan is what apply runs; a stale plan is refused.
  • The unit of a job is configurable: a whole shard by default, or N chunks.

docs.title: Commands and options
docs.text:
Option plan apply build INPUT, -o BUILD_DIR, --session ✔ ✔ ✔ --limits, --safety-margin, --threads ✔ ✔ --chunk-budget, --max-chunks ✔ ✔ --chunks-per-job N (new) ✔ --base-path, --skip-compression, --keep-previous ✔ ✔ --offline ✔ --cluster FILE (new) ✔ --pending (new: list jobs not done) ✔ --shard (filter what is planned) ✔ --task (select what is run: shards, tasks or jobs) ✔ --show-progress, --notify, --fail-fast ✔ ✔
  • apply --run is removed: --task replaces it.
  • build = plan then apply on the plan just written (whole shard jobs).

docs.title: Shards, chunks and jobs
docs.text:
plan describes the work as tasks, one per shard part (<shard>_<session>, where <shard> is <name>_g<n> or <name>_g<n>_p<m>). A task is one session's samples added to one shard:

  • its chunks: the kmtricks runs (<part> or <part>_chunk<n>);
  • its merge: check runs, merge, swap, register, check, clean up (what <shard>_merge.sh does today).

A task's work is grouped into jobs, what apply --task and a SLURM array task run. A job never spans tasks.

A plan task is not a SLURM task: the SLURM side is always written "array task". --chunks-per-job N sets the grouping:

N Jobs of a shard with c chunks 0 (default) one job <shard>: all chunks, then the merge N > 0, c <= N same as 0 N > 0, c > N ceil(c / N) jobs <shard>_j<k> of up to N chunks, then a job <shard>_merge after all of them

Chunks of one job run one after the other, each sized by --limits.

Example, shard idx_g0 in 7 chunks with --chunks-per-job 3:

idx_g0_j0     chunk0 chunk1 chunk2
idx_g0_j1     chunk3 chunk4 chunk5
idx_g0_j2     chunk6
idx_g0_merge  needs idx_g0_j0, idx_g0_j1, idx_g0_j2

docs.title: The plan bundle
docs.text:
Written to BUILD_DIR/assets/SESSION/, one directory per shard:

assets/initial/
  plan.yaml                       # session manifest (below)
  slurm/                          # with --cluster only (see Cluster)
    jobs.txt  build.sbatch  submit.sh
  idx_g0/
    idx_g0_initial.sh         # one script per chunk
    idx_g0_initial.fof        # its sample list
    merge.sh                      # the merge of the shard
    merge/                        # runs.tsv and the register .tsv of each merge step
    jobs/                         # only with --chunks-per-job N > 0
      j0.sh  j1.sh  merge.sh      # each calls `kmhelpers apply --task <job>`
  idx_g1/
    ...
  • Every file of a shard lives in its directory: a job never spans shards.
  • Run files keep the full run name (<part>_chunk<n>.sh), so a file name alone matches log lines and --task values.
  • With --chunks-per-job 0 there is no jobs/: the shard is the job (its run scripts, then merge.sh).
  • An index definition outside a span registry is its own target: it gets its own directory, named after it.
  • Logs follow the same layout: BUILD_DIR/logs/<shard>/ holds the kmtricks.log of its chunks and the logs of its merge.

plan.yaml:

type: plan
fingerprint: sha256:...        # see Staleness
created: 2026-10-23T10:00:00
definition: /data/db/compose/idx/initial/index.yaml
options:
  limits: {ram: 128849018880, threads: 24, ...}   # resolved values
  chunks_per_job: 3
  ...
tasks:
  idx_g0_initial:
    shard: idx_g0                 # target index in BUILD_DIR
    dir: idx_g0/
    samples: 448
    partitions: 64
    minim_size: 10
    threads: 24
    chunks:                         # dir/<chunk>.sh, dir/<chunk>.fof
      idx_g0_initial_chunk0: {samples: 64}
      ...
      idx_g0_initial_chunk6: {samples: 64}
    merge:
      script: merge.sh
      expects: {target_registered: false}   # or {partitions: 64, minim_size: 10}
      mode: merge                   # move: a single chunk and no current version
      max_inputs: 4
      steps:
        - {name: idx_g0__sub1_0, inputs: [idx_g0_initial_chunk0, ..., chunk3]}
        - {name: idx_g0__sub1_1, inputs: [idx_g0_initial_chunk4, ..., chunk6]}
        - {name: idx_g0, inputs: [idx_g0__sub1_0, idx_g0__sub1_1]}
    jobs:
      idx_g0_j0: [idx_g0_initial_chunk0, idx_g0_initial_chunk1, idx_g0_initial_chunk2]
      idx_g0_j1: [idx_g0_initial_chunk3, idx_g0_initial_chunk4, idx_g0_initial_chunk5]
      idx_g0_j2: [idx_g0_initial_chunk6]
      idx_g0_merge: [merge]       # after every other job of the shard

Done tests are implied: a chunk is done when its run directory is complete (chunk_problems), a merge when its done marker exists and the shard is registered.

docs.title: What plan decides
docs.text:
All the decisions IndexOps._run takes today, once, against the registry as it is at plan time:

  • partitions, threads, minimizer size, chunk split (resolve_build_params);
  • alignment with a registered target (IndexExecutor.align_with);
  • skip of definitions already registered or already in their target;
  • refusal of a part whose samples partly overlap its target;
  • move or merge, and the merge tree (MergeLimits, max_inputs, merge_tree);
  • the backup name of the replaced version.

Each decision that depends on the registry is written as expects on the shard's merge.

docs.title: What apply does
docs.text:
1. Load plan.yaml; fail if missing.
  2. Recompute the fingerprint; refuse if it differs ("plan is stale, run kmhelpers plan again").
  3. Select jobs: all (in dependency order), or those --task matches: a pattern matching a shard or a task selects all its jobs, one matching a job selects that job.
  4. For a <shard>_merge job, refuse if another job of the shard is not done.
  5. For each chunk, then the merge, of the job:
  6. done: skip (reused);
  7. chunk with an incomplete run directory: delete it, rebuild;
  8. merge: check expects against the live registry, refuse on mismatch (stale plan);
  9. run its script, log to BUILD_DIR/logs/<shard>/, stream it with --show-progress.
  10. Write the report (per task: each chunk's status, action, duration, kmtricks.log info; the merge details), updated after each step; --notify at exit.

Chunk and merge scripts are idempotent on their own (guards as merges have today), so running <shard>/<chunk>.sh or <shard>/merge.sh by hand is also safe.

docs.title: Staleness
docs.text:
The fingerprint hashes:

  • the definition file and COMPOSE_DIR/NAME/layout.yaml;
  • the resolved sample list (names and paths) of every planned definition;
  • the effective plan options (resolved limits, budgets, flags) and the --cluster file;
  • the kmhelpers version.

The registry is not hashed: it changes while jobs publish. It is checked per task merge through expects instead.

docs.title: Cluster (plan --cluster FILE)
docs.text:
--cluster takes a YAML file describing the scheduler and the resources of each kind of job. plan then writes the submission files next to the plan.

type: slurm                     # only slurm for now
partition: compute
time: 2-00:00:00
exclude: [node01]
account: null                   # optional: account, qos, constraint
max_parallel: 8                 # build array tasks running at once (%8)
output: logs/slurm/%x_%A_%a.out # relative to BUILD_DIR
setup: |                        # run before kmhelpers in every job
  export PATH=/path/to/kmhelpers/bin:$PATH
extra: []                       # other sbatch options, as is
jobs:                           # resources per kind of job
  build: {cpus: 24, mem: 120G}
  merge: {cpus: 24, mem: 120G}
  check: {cpus: 1, mem: 4G, time: "1:00:00"}
limits: {files: 131072, maps: 65530}  # optional: compute-node limits, see below
  • Keys under jobs.<kind> override the top-level ones (partition, time, ...) for that kind. Unknown keys are an error.
  • The cluster file is the source of the limits: plan sizes chunks from jobs.build (threads = cpus, ram = mem) and merges from jobs.merge, plus limits: for what the allocation does not tell. The allocation cannot differ from the plan. --limits with --cluster is an error.
  • limits.files and limits.maps are node settings, not part of an allocation. Without limits:, plan detects them on the node it runs on; set them only when the compute nodes differ from it:
  • files: the hard open-files limit (ulimit -Hn): kmhelpers and its scripts raise the soft limit to it (ulimit -Sn "$(ulimit -Hn)" in every generated script);
  • maps: vm.max_map_count (cat /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count), per node, not propagated by SLURM;
  • read them on a compute node with srun -p <partition> -c 1 --mem=1G -t 5 bash -c 'ulimit -Hn; cat /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count'.
  • The resolved file is copied into plan.yaml (cluster:) and hashed in the fingerprint.
  • The same file can be given in the -C config (plan: {cluster: ...}).

Writes slurm/:

jobs.txt          build jobs, one per line
build.sbatch      array: array task i runs `kmhelpers apply --task <line i>`
merge.sbatch      `kmhelpers apply --task <shard>_merge`
check.sbatch      `kmhelpers manage -r BUILD_DIR check`
submit.sh         submits what `apply --pending` lists (safe to run again):
                  1. the build array, %max_parallel
                  2. each merge job, --dependency=afterok:<array>_<array task
                     ids of its shard>
                  3. the check job, after every merge
  • With --chunks-per-job 0 there is no merge job: one array task per shard, no dependency; the check job waits for the whole array.
  • An array longer than the cluster MaxArraySize is split by submit.sh.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• apply sizing options, --run, and planning inside apply.
  • Parts registered separately by older kmhelpers (absorbed in IndexOps._publish and IndexExecutor.publish).
  • Old-layout symlinks: --keep-link on unregister, symlink resolution in IndexExecutor._remove.
  • kmhelpers_apply.sh and the flat <shard>.sh / <shard>_merge.sh / *.fof / *.tsv files: replaced by the per-shard directories.

docs.title: Implementation steps
docs.text:
1. IndexOps: build the plan (tasks, chunks, jobs, expects, fingerprint) without executing; write plan.yaml and the per-shard directories. Remove the legacy paths.
  2. Chunks: guard in each chunk script (complete run: skip, incomplete: rebuild), as merges are guarded.
  3. New executor for apply: load, check fingerprint, select, check needs/expects, run scripts, report, progress from logs.
  4. CLI: move options, add --chunks-per-job, --task, --pending, --cluster; build = plan + apply.
  5. --cluster: schema and validation, limits from the job resources, SLURM writer.
  6. Tests: e2e plan/apply/resume, stale plan, expects mismatch, job grouping (N = 0, N >= c, N < c), cluster file validation, SLURM files.
  7. Docs: commands/plan.md, apply.md, build.md.

docs.title: Dev environment setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/sebllns/kmhelpers
cd kmhelpers
pip install -e ".[dev]"

kmindex and kmtricks must also be available, see Installation.

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
pykmhelpers/
  cli/          # Click commands (one file per command)
  core/         # Low-level building blocks (index, bloom_filter, kmindex_wrapper, ...)
  operations/   # Higher-level operations (builder, fof_validation, ...)
  tests/        # Test suite
  pipeline/     # Pipeline execution engine

Each CLI command in cli/ is a thin layer that delegates to operations/ or core/.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
pytest

Coverage is reported automatically (configured in pyproject.toml). HTML report is written to htmlcov/.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
Tool Purpose black Formatting (line length 88) flake8 Linting mypy Type checking 
black pykmhelpers/
flake8 pykmhelpers/
mypy pykmhelpers/

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
Branch Purpose Updated by main Development trunk, always passing CI; releases are tags vX.Y.Z on it PR feature/<name>, fix/<name>, doc/<name>, ci/<name>, release/vX.Y.Z Short-lived work, deleted after merge Direct push docs Hidden docs preview, for docs work in progress Direct push paper JOSS paper; paper.pdf is committed by CI Direct push gh-pages Generated by the docs workflow, never edited by hand CI

main is protected: changes land through pull requests. Users install from tags, PyPI or bioconda, not from main.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
git checkout main
git pull
git checkout -b feature/my-feature
# ... commit ...
git push -u origin feature/my-feature
gh pr create --base main
# after review and green CI:
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch    # or --merge to keep each commit

Rules:

  • One branch per topic, from an up-to-date main, deleted after merge.
  • To bring new main commits into a pushed branch, use git merge main; rebase only before the first push.
  • git push --force-with-lease only on your own, unshared branch.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Docs are versioned with mike on the gh-pages branch, deployed by .github/workflows/docs.yml:

Trigger Deployed as URL Push to docs Hidden preview /kmhelpers/preview/ Push to main Version main, titled main (<short hash>), overwritten each time /kmhelpers/main/ Tag vX.Y.Z Version X.Y.Z, alias latest (default) /kmhelpers/X.Y.Z/

Content specific to a release or to the development version goes between release-only or dev-only HTML comment markers; @VERSION@ inside a release block is replaced by the version (see scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py, used in docs/getting-started/installation.md). Release builds get DOCS_RELEASE=X.Y.Z from the workflow; to preview one locally:

DOCS_RELEASE=X.Y.Z mkdocs serve

To try docs changes before merging, push them to docs (git push --force origin HEAD:docs) and open the preview.

Manual deploy from any branch or tag (the branch must be pushed):

# Redeploy a release from its tag
gh workflow run docs.yml --ref vX.Y.Z

# Deploy a branch as a given version, without moving "latest"
gh workflow run docs.yml --ref fix/docs-typo -f version=X.Y.Z -f latest=false

# Deploy and remove an old version
gh workflow run docs.yml --ref vX.Y.Z -f delete_version=<old>

# Follow the run
gh run watch $(gh run list --workflow docs.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')

Without -f version, the version is the package version of the ref (main on main). latest defaults to true. A release version gets the release-only blocks, like a tag build.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: pykmhelpers/_version.py is the single source of the version. Commands below use VERSION=X.Y.Z.

docs.title: 1. Prepare
docs.text:
git checkout main
git pull
git checkout -b release/v$VERSION
  • Set __version__ = "X.Y.Z" in pykmhelpers/_version.py.
  • Add the ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section to CHANGELOG.md. It becomes the GitHub release notes, so it must be written before tagging.
pytest
rm -rf dist && python -m build && twine check dist/*
git commit -am "release: v$VERSION"
git push -u origin release/v$VERSION

docs.title: 2. Merge into main
docs.text:
gh pr create --base main --title "Release v$VERSION" --body "See CHANGELOG.md"
gh pr checks --watch
gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch

docs.title: 3. Tag
docs.text:
git checkout main
git pull
git tag -a v$VERSION -m "kmhelpers v$VERSION" \
    -m "Documentation: https://sebllns.github.io/kmhelpers/$VERSION/
Changelog: https://sebllns.github.io/kmhelpers/$VERSION/changelog/"
git push origin v$VERSION

Or with git create-release (scripts/git-create-release, requires gh), which runs the commands above after checks, then lists the release workflow runs:

git create-release [--view] [--overwrite] [VERSION]

VERSION defaults to pykmhelpers/_version.py; a different one asks for confirmation. Before tagging, it checks that CHANGELOG.md has the ## [VERSION] section, that the tag does not exist, that the working tree is clean and that HEAD is origin/main.

Option Effect --view Show the release and the workflow runs, no tagging --overwrite Delete the GitHub release and the tag, then tag again -h Help (--help is caught by git for aliases)

The alias is defined in the versioned .gitconfig, enable it once per clone:

git config include.path ../.gitconfig

Never move or re-create a pushed tag, except with --overwrite when the release failed before the PyPI upload.

docs.title: 4. Automatic steps
docs.text:
Pushing the tag runs:

  • release.yml: builds the sdist and wheel, creates the GitHub release with the files attached and notes made of .github/release-notes.md (docs links, install and update commands), the CHANGELOG section and the merged PRs, then uploads the files to PyPI (publish job) and installs the published version in a fresh environment to check kmhelpers --version (verify job).
  • docs.yml: deploys the docs as version X.Y.Z with alias latest.
gh run list --limit 4
gh release view v$VERSION    # or: git create-release --view

docs.title: 5. Approve the PyPI upload (browser)
docs.text:
The publish job runs in the pypi environment, which waits for a manual approval:

  1. Open the "Release build" run of the tag in the Actions tab.
  2. Once tests and build are green, check the release: notes, sdist and wheel attached.
  3. Click "Review deployments", select pypi, then "Approve and deploy".
  4. When publish and verify are green, check the version on PyPI and the docs at https://sebllns.github.io/kmhelpers/X.Y.Z/.

A PyPI version cannot be uploaded twice: a broken release is fixed by a new version.

docs.title: 6. Bioconda
docs.text: After the PyPI upload, the bioconda bot opens a PR in bioconda-recipes updating the version and sha256. Check that runtime dependencies still match pyproject.toml, then approve it.

docs.title: Patch of an older version
docs.text:
Only when a fix must be released for a version older than main. The tag is created manually, as git create-release only tags origin/main:

git checkout -b maint/vX.Y v$OLD_VERSION
# commit the fix, bump the version, add the CHANGELOG section
git push -u origin maint/vX.Y
git tag -a v$PATCH_VERSION -m "kmhelpers v$PATCH_VERSION"
git push origin v$PATCH_VERSION

Then bring the fix and the CHANGELOG section into main through a PR. This tag gets the latest docs alias; redeploy the newest release afterwards with gh workflow run docs.yml --ref v<newest>.

docs.title: Building the Documentation
docs.text: The docs are built with MkDocs using the Material theme.

docs.title: Install dependencies
docs.text:
For development:

pip install -e ".[dev]"

For docs only:

pip install -e ".[docs]"

docs.title: Live preview
docs.text:
Starts a local server with hot-reload on file changes:

mkdocs serve --dirtyreload --livereload

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser.

docs.title: Build static site
docs.text:
Outputs the static HTML to site/:

mkdocs build

The site/ directory is git-ignored and should not be committed.

docs.title: Adding or editing pages
docs.text:
1. Edit or create a .md file under docs/.
  2. If it's a new page, add it to the nav: section in mkdocs.yml.
  3. Run mkdocs serve to preview.

docs.title: Release banner
docs.text: The home page shows a dismissible banner announcing the current release, set in the announce block of overrides/main.html. Update its text at each release (or empty the block to remove it); a reader who closed it sees it again once the text changes.

docs.title: Deploying to GitHub Pages
docs.text: Docs are versioned with mike. Do not use mkdocs gh-deploy - it overwrites the entire gh-pages branch and destroys version history.

docs.title: Deploy a new version
docs.text:
mike deploy --push --update-aliases <version> latest

Example for a release:

mike deploy --push --update-aliases 0.8.0 latest

This builds the docs, pushes them to gh-pages under /<version>/, and updates the latest alias to point to it.

docs.title: List deployed versions
docs.text: mike list

docs.title: Preview versioned docs locally
docs.text: mike serve

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
New to kmhelpers?

Start here: install the toolkit, then walk through the pipeline with a quick, hands-on example.

  1. Installation: set up kmhelpers and its dependencies (kmindex, kmtricks, ntCard) via Conda
  2. Quick Start: learn the design → build → query pipeline and common use cases
  3. Tutorial: Once you're set up, walk through a full, real-data example end to end.
  4. Concepts: the words used in this documentation (shard, partition, session, chunk...), and how an index is structured and built.

By Glosome - Own work, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Once kmhelpers is installed, the fastest way to get hands-on is the E. coli tutorial - it builds a queryable index from real data in three commands. For syntax and options on any command, see the Command Reference.

Tip

kh is available as a short alias for kmhelpers - both commands are identical.

docs.title: The Pipeline
docs.text:
kmhelpers exposes the index lifecycle as a sequence of commands, illustrated in figure below:

Command breakdown
  • list - recursively discovers all samples in a given directory and counts each sample's distinct \(k\)-mers using ntcard (unless the counts are provided by the user).
  • profile - determines the best set of sub-index BF sizes given the user-defined maximum number of sub-indexes and target false-positive rate.
  • compose - assigns each sample to its sub-index and generates the files-of-files describing the data origin of each sub-index.
  • plan - validates sample files, available disk space, and memory upfront, and emits ready-to-execute pipeline scripts.
  • apply - builds all sub-indexes by invoking kmindex, with span-level and name-level filtering.

For ease of use, steps list, profile, and compose can be grouped under a single command named design, and steps plan and apply can be grouped under the build command.

Once an index is built, kmhelpers also answers queries (query). Multi-step workflows can be described as declarative YAML pipelines (pipeline) and executed in a single command.

An additional command, manage (under development), lets users register several distinct indexes (built locally or hosted anywhere accessible) into one logical index, redirecting each query to all registered indexes at query time.

Indices are built and queried in three steps:

[1] design → [2] build → [3] query
Step Command Purpose Input Output 1 design Discover samples and generate index definitions directory or sample list index definitions 2 build Build k-mer indices from those definitions index definitions built k-mer index 3 query Search the indices with FASTA/FASTQ sequences built index + query sequences match results

docs.title: Create a new index
docs.text:
Turn a collection of samples into a searchable index, from nothing. Input: your sequence files. Output: a queryable index.

Run the pipeline steps against a directory of sequence files (or a plain-text / YAML sample list):

Commands 
kmhelpers design /data/sequences -o coli_db/ -n coli
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/

Your index is ready to query:

Commands 
kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ -o results/ query.fa

See the E. coli tutorial for a full walkthrough.

docs.title: Update an existing index
docs.text:
Add new samples to an index you already built, without starting over. Input: an existing index, plus the new samples to add. Output: the same index, now also containing the new samples.

Re-run design with the same -o/-n and a new sample source, tagging the run with a fresh -s session ID:

Commands 
kmhelpers design coli_5_update.txt -o coli_db/ -n coli -s update
kmhelpers build coli_db -s update -o coli_build/

design detects the existing layout file at coli_db/compose/coli/layout.yaml, skips the profile step, and composes only the new samples. build then merges the new samples into the existing index automatically, without recounting the samples already indexed.

Disk space

kmindex cannot add samples to an existing index in place, so the update merges the previous samples and the new ones into a complete new index, which replaces the previous one in its folder (coli_build/coli_g0/). Both versions coexist on disk during the merge, so plan for at least twice the size of the sub-indices being updated.

The previous version is deleted once the updated one is registered and checked; --keep-previous keeps it to compare both - see build - Updating an index.

docs.title: Query sequences in an index
docs.text:
Check whether given sequences are present in your samples. Input: a built index, plus the sequences you want to search for. Output: for each sequence, which samples it was found in.

Point query at a built registry (-r) with one or more FASTA/FASTQ files, directories, or stdin:

Commands 
# Query the whole index (all sub-indices)
kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ -o results/ query.fa

# Query specific sub-indices with multiple threads
kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ --sh coli_g0 --sh coli_g1 -t 4 -o results/ query.fa

# Scan a directory of query files, or read from stdin
kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ -o results/ ./queries_dir/
cat query.fa | kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ -o results/ -

See query for batching, output formats, and threshold options.

docs.title: Work with large datasets: automatic vs manual build
docs.text:
Build large indices safely and faster, by checking the work before it runs and spreading it across multiple machines. Input: the same index definitions produced by design or compose. Output: the same built index, produced manually step-by-step for more flexibility.

For large sample counts, prefer running plan and apply separately instead of build (which chains them). plan validates all sample paths and writes ready-to-run shell scripts to OUTPUT_DIR/assets/SESSION/ up front, so path errors surface before any CPU/I/O-intensive building starts:

Commands 
kmhelpers plan coli_db -o coli_build/

Automatic build

Review the plan in coli_build/assets/initial/ (plan.yaml and one folder of scripts per shard) and the plan report in coli_build/logs/ (see build - Report), then:

Commands 
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/

Manual build

The plan is made of plain bash scripts, in OUTPUT_DIR/assets/SESSION/<shard>/: one per kmtricks run (<part>.sh, or <part>_chunk<N>.sh), then merge.sh (check, publish, cleanup). They can be run by hand for a fully hands-on build, runs first, then the merge:

Commands 
kmhelpers plan coli_db -o coli_build/
for shard in coli_build/assets/initial/*/; do
    for run in "$shard"*.sh; do [ "$run" = "${shard}merge.sh" ] || bash "$run"; done
    bash "${shard}merge.sh"
done

On a cluster, plan --cluster cluster.yaml sizes the plan for the jobs of cluster.yaml and writes the SLURM files submitting them, with --chunks-per-job to spread the chunks of a shard over several nodes (see plan - Cluster). apply runs any subset of the jobs (--task: shards or jobs), lists those not done (--pending), and can email a notification on completion:

Commands 
kmhelpers plan coli_db -o coli_build/ --cluster cluster.yaml
bash coli_build/assets/initial/slurm/submit.sh

# or by hand, each node a disjoint subset, emailing when its share is done
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --task coli_g0 --notify you@example.com
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/ --task coli_g1 --notify you@example.com

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone --branch vv0.8.0.dev0 https://github.com/sebllns/kmhelpers
cd kmhelpers

docs.title: 2. Create the Conda environment
docs.text:
conda env create -f conda/environment.yml -p ./.env

This installs kmindex, ntcard, and all Python dependencies into a local .env directory.

docs.title: 3. Activate the environment
docs.text:
conda activate ./.env

Note

Run this activation command each time you open a new terminal session before using kmhelpers.

Tip

You can install to a permanent location instead:

conda env create -f conda/environment.yml -p ~/.kmhelpers
conda activate ~/.kmhelpers

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
kmhelpers --version
kmhelpers --help

Verify dependencies:

kmindex --version
kmtricks --version
ntcard --version

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
From the repository root:

git fetch --tags
git checkout vv0.8.0.dev0
conda env update -f conda/environment.yml -p ./.env --prune

Then verify the installed version:

kmhelpers --version

docs.title: Tutorial: Indexing 10 E. coli Assemblies
docs.text: By the end you will have a queryable k-mer index of these assemblies built in three commands: design → build → query.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• kmhelpers installed (see Installation)
  • Command wget to download the dataset
  • ~200 MB of free disk space for the dataset + resulting index

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The following tools are installed alongside kmhelpers when using the conda environment:

  • kmindex - the underlying indexing engine
  • ntcard - k-mer counter used by list

docs.title: Step 1 - Download the dataset
docs.text:
mkdir -p coli_dataset && cd coli_dataset
wget "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/000/780/515/GCA_000780515.1_ASM78051v1/GCA_000780515.1_ASM78051v1_genomic.fna.gz"
wget "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/001/076/125/GCA_001076125.1_ASM107612v1/GCA_001076125.1_ASM107612v1_genomic.fna.gz"

cd ..
I/O

Input: 10 NCBI FTP URLs Output: coli_dataset/

docs.title: Step 2 - Create a file list
docs.text:
cat > coli_10.txt << 'EOF'
coli_dataset/GCA_000780515.1_ASM78051v1_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_001076125.1_ASM107612v1_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_001417575.1_ASM141757v1_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_000944435.1_Ec57A_E8C1_MIRA_assembly_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_001075925.1_ASM107592v1_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_000936715.1_E8C1_assembly_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_000939215.1_Ec57A_A7_MIRA_assembly_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_001413795.1_ASM141379v1_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_001373195.1_57A_A7_assembly_genomic.fna.gz
coli_dataset/GCA_000938575.1_D1C4_assembly_genomic.fna.gz
EOF
I/O

Input: paths to the 10 .fna.gz files (written manually) Output: coli_10.txt

docs.title: Step 3 - Design the index (design)
docs.text:
kmhelpers design coli_10.txt \
    -o coli_db/ \
    -n coli \
    -s initial \
    -k 25 \
    -b 1.1 \
    -g 2 \
    --sb 0
I/O

Input: coli_10.txt Output: coli_db/list/ (JSONL), coli_db/profile/ (profile.yaml, groups.png), coli_db/compose/ (index definitions)

Options Option Meaning coli_10.txt INPUT: the sample files, one path per line -o coli_db/ design directory: receives list/, profile/ and compose/ -n coli index name: its sub-indexes are coli_g0, coli_g1 -s initial session: this first set of samples; an update adds a session (see Update the index) -k 25 k-mer size (default: 25) -b 1.1 span base: samples are bucketed by k-mer count, in steps of x1.1 (see profile) -g 2 2 storage-balanced groups, one sub-index each (-g 0, the default, chooses the number) --sb 0 no sharding: each group is one index. A shard budget splits a large group into independent shards (coli_g0_p0, ...), see compose - Sharding

Not set here: the data type, assembled by default (--dt u for raw reads), and the false-positive rate --fp 0.25.

INFO

design runs list → profile → compose in a single command. For a detailed walkthrough of each sub-command, see Step-by-step: list → profile → compose.

docs.title: Step 4 - Build the index (build)
docs.text:
kmhelpers build coli_db -o coli_build/ --cb 0 --show-progress
I/O

Input: coli_db/compose/coli/initial/index.yaml Output: coli_build/index.json + one folder per sub-index, coli_build/coli_g0/ and coli_build/coli_g1/ - ready-to-query index

Options Option Meaning coli_db INPUT: the design directory; its last session is built (-s picks another) -o coli_build/ index directory (BUILD_DIR): receives the indices, reused by updates, passed to query -r --cb 0 no chunk budget: each shard is built by one kmtricks run. Otherwise a large shard is built in chunks, then merged (see build - Shards and chunks) --show-progress one line per shard: progress bar, step running, end status (see apply - Following a build)

Not set here: the resources, detected on this machine (--limits to set them). On a cluster, --hpc cluster.yaml plans the build for SLURM jobs and submits them (see build - On a cluster).

INFO

build runs plan → apply in a single command, validating all paths before starting the build. For a detailed walkthrough, or to run plan first and apply later with bash or apply, see Step-by-step: plan → apply.

docs.title: Step 5 - Query the index (query)
docs.text:
Extract the first contig of the first sample as a query sequence:

zcat coli_dataset/GCA_000780515.1_ASM78051v1_genomic.fna.gz \
    | awk '/^>/{n++} n==2{exit} {print}' > query.fa

Then query the index:

kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ -o results/ query.fa
I/O

Input: coli_build/ (index root), query.fa (first contig of GCA_000780515) Output: results/

Options Option Meaning -r coli_build/ the index directory to query (BUILD_DIR of build) -o results/ output directory: one folder per query file query.fa the query file(s), FASTA or FASTQ, gzipped or not

Not set here: -z 6 (findere: (k+z)-mers, which lowers the false-positive rate), --thr 0.05 (minimum score reported), -f tsv (results format). See query.

RESULT

query merges the results of all sub-indices into results/query/results.tsv, one row per query sequence and one column per matching sample:

seq GCA_000780515_1_ASM78051v1_genomic_fna
JSPL01000060.1  1.000

Each value is the fraction of query k-mers found in that sample. Samples scoring below the threshold (--thr, default 0.05) are omitted. Use -f to select another output format (json, yaml, md, html). GCA_000780515 scores 1.0 -- a perfect match, as expected since query.fa was extracted from that assembly.

docs.text:

docs.title: Step-by-step: list → profile → compose → plan → apply
docs.text: This page is a companion to the E. coli tutorial. It assumes you have already followed the main steps and are looking for a deeper understanding of what each sub-command does, or want to run stages individually to inspect or re-run a specific part of the pipeline.

docs.title: design
docs.text: The three steps below are equivalent to Step 3 of the tutorial.

docs.title: Step 3.1 - Scan samples and count k-mers (list)
docs.text:
mkdir -p coli_db/list
kmhelpers list coli_10.txt -o coli_db/list/coli.jsonl -k 25
I/O

Input: coli_10.txt Output: coli_db/list/coli.jsonl

Options Option Meaning coli_10.txt INPUT: the sample files, one path per line -o coli_db/list/coli.jsonl the sample list written (JSONL) -k 25 k-mer size counted by ntcard (default: 25)

Not set here: the data type, assembled by default (--dt u for raw reads).

INFO

list reads each path, counts k-mers with ntcard (k = 25), and writes one JSONL record per sample to coli_db/list/coli.jsonl.

RESULT

The header line records the shared parameters; every subsequent line is one sample:

{"description": "Generated by kmhelpers list", "date": "2026-06-29T12:58:33.254120", "root_path": "/root_path", "k": 25, "assembled": true, "abundance_min": 1}
{"name": "GCA_000780515_1_ASM78051v1_genomic_fna", "files": ["/home/sbelleno/work/data/tuto_kmhelpers_v2/coli_dataset/GCA_000780515.1_ASM78051v1_genomic.fna.gz"], "kmer_count": 10898876}
{"name": "GCA_001076125_1_ASM107612v1_genomic_fna", "files": ["/home/sbelleno/work/data/tuto_kmhelpers_v2/coli_dataset/GCA_001076125.1_ASM107612v1_genomic.fna.gz"], "kmer_count": 10180102}
...

docs.title: Step 3.2 - Profile the k-mer distribution (profile)
docs.text:
kmhelpers profile coli_db/list/coli.jsonl -o coli_db/profile/ -b 1.1 -g 2
I/O

Input: coli_db/list/coli.jsonl Output: coli_db/profile/profile.yaml, coli_db/profile/groups.png

Options Option Meaning coli_db/list/coli.jsonl INPUT: the sample list of list -o coli_db/profile/ output directory: profile.yaml, groups.png -b 1.1 span base: samples are bucketed by k-mer count, in steps of x1.1 -g 2 2 storage-balanced groups, one sub-index each (-g 0, the default, chooses the number)

Not set here: the false-positive rate --fp 0.25.

INFO

A span is an integer bucket that summarises a sample's k-mer count:

\[ s = \left\lfloor \log_{\text{base}}(n) \right\rfloor \]

where \(n\) is the sample's distinct k-mer count. All samples whose k-mer count falls in the same bucket \([\text{base}^s,\, \text{base}^{s+1})\) share span \(s\) and are indexed together in one sub-index.

The Bloom filter allocated for that sub-index is sized for the worst case of the bucket - the maximum k-mer count \(\text{base}^{s+1}\) - so every sample in the span fits:

\[ \text{bf_size} = \left\lceil \frac{f \cdot \text{base}^{s+1}}{8} \right\rceil \times 8 \qquad \text{where } f = \frac{-\ln p}{(\ln 2)^2} \]

\(p\) is the false-positive rate (default 0.25) and the \(\times 8\) rounding aligns the size to a byte boundary.

False-positive rate and findere

A higher \(p\) reduces Bloom-filter size and therefore disk footprint, at the cost of more false positives. At query time the findere algorithm compensates by querying \((k+z)\)-mers instead of \(k\)-mers, reducing the effective false-positive rate to \(p^z\):

\[ p_{\text{eff}} = p^z \]

Recommended settings: build with --fp 0.25 (default), query with -z 6 (default), giving \(0.25^6 \approx 0.024\,\%\) effective FP rate.

Lucas Robidou and Pierre Peterlongo. findere: fast and precise approximate membership query. SPIRE 2021, Springer, pp. 151–163. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-86692-1_13

Choosing base and the number of groups

base controls bucket width. With base=2.0 (default) each bucket spans a 2× range of k-mer counts, producing few coarse spans. -b 1.1 narrows each bucket to a 10 % range, giving finer resolution at the cost of more spans. -g 2 then requests that those spans be merged into 2 groups. For a dataset this small and uniform, -g 1 (a single group) would actually be the optimal choice; we use -g 2 here to illustrate how grouping works - pick a value that fits your own distribution.

RESULT

profile writes three output files to coli_profile/:

profile.yaml

Records global parameters and one named profile per grouping. The baseline profile preserves the natural 5-span distribution; 2_groups merges them into two sub-indices:

false_positive_rate: 0.25
span_base: 1.1
sample_count: 10
biggest_sample: ('GCA_000780515_1_ASM78051v1', 10898876)
max_kmer_count: 11971516
default_profile: 2_groups
profiles:
baseline:
    span_list: [161, 167, 168, 169, 170]
    bloom_size: [14649392, 25952288, 28547520, 31402272, 34542496]
    sample_dist: [5, 1, 2, 1, 1]
    disk_usage: [1.47e+07B, 2.6e+07B, 2.86e+07B, 3.14e+07B, 3.46e+07B]
    size_ratio: ['0.109', '0.192', '0.211', '0.232', '0.256']
    total_size: 1.35e+08B
    bytes_per_sample: 1.35e+07B
2_groups:
    span_list: [161, 170]
    bloom_size: [14649392, 34542496]
    sample_dist: [5, 5]
    disk_usage: [1.47e+07B, 3.46e+07B]
    size_ratio: ['0.298', '0.702']
    total_size: 4.92e+07B
    bytes_per_sample: 4.92e+06B
groups.png

A plot showing the k-mer count distribution, natural span boundaries, and the requested 2-group overlay.

Grouping affects both storage and query performance.

Storage

kmindex stores samples in packs of 8 (bit-packing), so a sub-index with 1 sample occupies the same disk space as one with 8. In the baseline profile, spans 167, 169 and 170 hold only 1–2 samples each - those near-empty packs waste most of their allocated space, bringing the total to 135 MB. In this case, merging the 5 sub-indices into 2 reduces the number of packs from 5 to 2 (one per group), cutting the total to 50 MB.

Query time

Each sub-index is composed of multiple partition files (kmindex terminology). Query performance on large datasets is dominated by disk latency rather than CPU, so every sub-index multiplies the number of partitions that must be opened and read. Fewer sub-indices means fewer partition files accessed per query, directly reducing that latency overhead.

docs.title: Step 3.3 - Compose index definitions (compose)
docs.text:
kmhelpers compose coli_db/list/coli.jsonl \
    -o coli_db/compose/ \
    -n coli \
    -s initial \
    --pf coli_db/profile/profile.yaml \
    --sb 0
I/O

Input: coli_db/list/coli.jsonl, coli_db/profile/profile.yaml Output: coli_db/compose/coli/initial/ (index.yaml and shards/), and the layout coli_db/compose/coli/layout.yaml

Options Option Meaning coli_db/list/coli.jsonl INPUT: the sample list -o coli_db/compose/ compose directory: one folder per index -n coli, -s initial index name, and session --pf coli_db/profile/profile.yaml the profile of profile: its groups become the sub-indexes --sb 0 no sharding: each group is one index. A shard budget splits a large group into independent shards (coli_g0_p0, ...), see compose - Sharding INFO

compose reads the sample list and the profile, then writes index definition files into coli_db/compose/coli/initial/: index.yaml summarises the session and its shards. Pass coli_db to plan, build or apply in the next step. The sample-to-sub-index repartition is driven by the selected profile - here 2_groups, the default set by profile - whose Bloom-filter sizes are read from coli_db/profile/profile.yaml.

docs.title: build
docs.text: The two steps below are equivalent to Step 4 of the tutorial.

docs.title: Step 4.1 - Preview the build plan (plan)
docs.text:
kmhelpers plan coli_db -o coli_build/ --cb 0
I/O

Input: coli_db/compose/coli/initial/index.yaml Output: build scripts in coli_build/assets/initial/ + report in coli_build/logs/

Options Option Meaning coli_db INPUT: the design directory; its last session is planned (-s picks another) -o coli_build/ index directory: the plan is written to coli_build/assets/initial/ --cb 0 no chunk budget: each shard is built by one kmtricks run. Otherwise a large shard is built in chunks, then merged (see build - Shards and chunks)

Every build decision is taken here (partitions, threads, chunks, merges), from the resources of this machine (--limits to set them): apply takes no such option. --hpc cluster.yaml plans for SLURM jobs instead (see plan - Cluster).

INFO

Before committing to a potentially long build, validate paths and preview the commands that will be executed: plan checks that every sample file exists, reports any missing paths, and writes the equivalent kmtricks and kmindex commands - without running them. Fix any path errors now rather than discovering them mid-build.

RESULT Report in coli_build/logs/kmhelpers_plan_<timestamp>.yaml
  • summary -- status (SUCCESS, PARTIAL, FAILED), counts, and totals: shards, samples, kmtricks runs, estimated size, also per span
  • kmindex / kmhelpers / system -- tool versions, host, and the SLURM job if any
  • limits -- the RAM, open files and threads the build is sized for
  • shards -- one entry per sub-index (coli_g0, coli_g1) and its part of this session: sample count, build parameters (threads, partitions), estimated size, scripts, the kmtricks runs to build, and how it will be published

apply writes the same report, completed with what happened (run durations, peak memory, size on disk); see build - Report.

The plan in coli_build/assets/initial/
  • plan.yaml -- what apply runs: one task per sub-index, its kmtricks runs, its merge and its jobs (see plan).
  • coli_g<span>/coli_g<span>_initial.sh -- one script per kmtricks run (or chunk) of the sub-index (coli_g0, coli_g1), with Bloom-filter size, k-mer size, partitions and threads pre-filled, next to its sample list (.fof).
  • coli_g<span>/merge.sh -- checks the runs, publishes them as the sub-index (moved in place, or merged), checks it, then deletes the runs. Each script stops at the first failing command and can be run again; see build - Builds and merges.

docs.title: Step 4.2 - Build the index (apply or bash)
docs.text:
applybash 
kmhelpers apply coli_db -o coli_build/
I/O

Input: coli_db/compose/coli/initial/index.yaml Output: coli_build/index.json + one folder per sub-index, coli_build/coli_g0/ and coli_build/coli_g1/ - ready-to-query index

Options Option Meaning coli_db the INPUT given to plan -o coli_build/ the index directory given to plan: apply runs its plan

--status shows where the build stands, --task runs part of it, --show-progress draws one line per shard (see apply).

for shard in coli_g0 coli_g1; do
    bash coli_build/assets/initial/$shard/${shard}_initial.sh
    bash coli_build/assets/initial/$shard/merge.sh
done
I/O

Input: coli_build/assets/initial/<shard>/*.sh Output: coli_build/index.json + one folder per sub-index, coli_build/coli_g0/ and coli_build/coli_g1/ - ready-to-query index

RESULT

Once complete, the index is registered in coli_build/index.json and ready to query.

docs.title: Update an existing index: design → build
docs.text: This page is a companion to the E. coli tutorial. It shows how to add samples to an index that already exists, without rebuilding it from scratch. It assumes you have already followed the main steps and have coli_db/ and coli_build/ on disk.

docs.title: Step 1 - Download a new sample
docs.text:
cd coli_dataset
wget "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/000/005/845/GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2/GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz"
cd ..
I/O

Input: one NCBI FTP URL (E. coli K-12 MG1655 reference assembly) Output: coli_dataset/GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz

docs.title: Step 2 - Create a file list for the new samples
docs.text:
cat > coli_update.txt << 'EOF'
coli_dataset/GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz
EOF
I/O

Input: path to the new .fna.gz file Output: coli_update.txt

INFO

List only the new samples. Samples already indexed must not be repeated.

docs.title: Step 3 - Design the update session (design)
docs.text:
Re-run design with the same -o and -n as Step 3 of the tutorial, and a fresh -s session ID:

kmhelpers design coli_update.txt -o coli_db/ -n coli -s update
I/O

Input: coli_update.txt, existing layout coli_db/compose/coli/layout.yaml Output: coli_db/compose/coli/update/index.yaml

Options Option Meaning coli_update.txt INPUT: the new sample files -o coli_db/, -n coli the design directory and index of the first session -s update a new session: its samples are added to the existing sub-indexes

Not set here, and not to be: -k, -b, -g and --sb come from the layout of the index (coli_db/compose/coli/layout.yaml), so the update fits the existing sub-indexes.

INFO

design detects the existing layout file at coli_db/compose/coli/layout.yaml, skips the profile step, and composes only the new samples. The k-mer size, span base and grouping of the initial run are reused, so the new sub-indices stay compatible with the existing ones.

docs.title: Step 4 - Build the update session (build)
docs.text:
Build into the same BUILD_DIR as Step 4 of the tutorial:

kmhelpers build coli_db -s update -o coli_build/ --cb 0 --show-progress
I/O

Input: coli_db/compose/coli/update/index.yaml Output: updated coli_g0 in coli_build/coli_g0/, updated coli_build/index.json

Options Option Meaning coli_db, -s update the design directory, and the session to build -o coli_build/ the same index directory as the first build: the new samples are merged into its sub-indexes --cb 0 no chunk budget: one kmtricks run per shard (see build - Shards and chunks) --show-progress one line per shard: progress bar, step running, end status INFO

Each index keeps its folder, coli_build/<name>/. While the session is built, its runs and merges live in coli_build/work/update/, deleted at the end. Building the same session again resumes it, or does nothing if it finished.

Building a session into a BUILD_DIR that already holds the index triggers a merge. kmindex cannot add samples to an existing index in place, so the update merges the old and the new samples into a new index, which replaces the previous one in coli_build/coli_g0/: it now holds its initial samples plus the new one. The previous version is deleted once the new one is checked (--keep-previous keeps it in coli_build/work/update/previous/).

GCA_000005845 falls in the span bucket of coli_g0, so only that sub-index is merged. coli_g1 is untouched.

Disk space

The previous version and the updated one coexist on disk during the merge. Plan for at least twice the size of the sub-indices being updated.

docs.title: Step 5 - Query the updated index (query)
docs.text:
kmhelpers query -r coli_build/ -o results_update/ query.fa
Options Option Meaning -r coli_build/ the updated index directory -o results_update/ another output directory, to compare with results/ query.fa the same query as before RESULT

coli_g0 now holds 6 samples, the 5 initial ones plus GCA_000005845. query.fa comes from GCA_000780515, indexed in coli_g1, which still scores 1.0.

The previous version was deleted once the updated one was registered and checked. To compare both versions, build with --keep-previous: the previous coli_g0 is then left in coli_build/work/update/previous/coli_g0/, to delete once done.

docs.title: Step 6 - Check the result
docs.text:
# Registered indices and the samples they hold
kmhelpers manage -r coli_build/ list
kmhelpers manage -r coli_build/ info --sh coli_g0
kmhelpers manage -r coli_build/ check
Options Option Meaning -r coli_build/ the index directory (registry) list the registered sub-indexes and their sample counts info --sh coli_g0 details of one sub-index: samples, partitions, size check checks every sub-index on disk against the registry
